- **S3K springs now preserve their native init-only SST execution:** `Obj_Spring` installs its directional routine and returns before any solid or proactive-trigger logic can run, preventing a newly loaded CNZ horizontal spring from launching CPU Tails one frame early (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:47500-47652`).
- **CNZ2's magnetic end boss now runs its locked-on-ROM encounter path:** the camera-range gate installs PLC `$6E` art and `Pal_CNZEndBoss`, starts boss music, then advances through the native swing, player tracking, magnet drop/bounce, alignment, charge, attraction, descent, and return phases. The ship uses its high-priority layer and mapped frame, hit handling retains the 32-frame palette-flash window, and defeat uses the stored-bound `$190`/`$310` camera writes before the existing capsule, cannon, and ICZ handoffs (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:145801-146765`).
- **CNZ's late water cork no longer arms the final water button:** the cork helper writes its native `_unkFAA2` latch and `$958` target without inventing an `_unkFAA3` write; the distinct button-arm flag remains owned by the earlier cutscene button (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:133988,134030-134083`).
- **CNZ sprite ordering now follows the locked-on ROM object attributes:** balloons, light bulbs, and cylinders use priority `$280` (bucket 5), while Clamer, Sparkle, and Batbot retain their high-plane art flags, including inherited badnik child art (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:66747-66755,67257-67264,67614-67640,185861-186388`).
- Fix(s3k): Bonus-stage entry now reads the recorded controller input on its first gameplay frame, and the ring carry-over on exit matches the ROM. (1) The BONUS title-card-exit fall-through frame is the interior's first gameplay tick, but `PlaybackDebugManager.isDriving` drives the forced-input bridge only in LEVEL/BONUS_STAGE, so the step-top `syncPlaybackInputBridge` (running while the mode was still TITLE_CARD) left that first tick with a neutral/stale input. `GameLoop.exitTitleCard` now re-arms the forced-input bridge immediately after flipping to BONUS_STAGE (bonus-entry branch only; LEVEL title-card exits are unaffected), so the player's first interior tick reads the frame it should -- for the gumball, the recorded frame-0 grounded left ground-move (air-forced-false for one frame -> `g_speed` -0x0C -> then falls into the machine) instead of an immediate air-accel free-fall that diverged the whole fall. (2) `GameLoop.doExitBonusStage` restores the returning level's ring count from the interior's live HUD `Ring_count` captured before the reload (ROM `loc_61076`: `move.w (Ring_count).w,(Saved_ring_count).w`, docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:127760), matching the ROM's exit copy that discards the transient `+20` a gumball ring ball adds to `Saved_ring_count` while only `+10` reaches the HUD (loc_6114E:127845); the former `savedRingCount + rewards.rings()` returned 79 rings where the ROM returns 69. (3) `GameLoop.updateBonusStageMode`'s exit-fade freeze branch now advances the shared playback cursor + VBla counter each frozen frame, mirroring the ROM's V_int ticking across the post-catch BONUS_STAGE tail. Drives `TestS3kMegaRunChain`'s gumball interior from 3709 comparator errors (stage exit never observed) to 9 errors with the stage exit observed and ring carry-over correct, advancing the chain through the gumball round trip and the following aiz_2 segment. Verified against the six S3K stage comparators, `TestS1GhzMazeRoundTripChain`, `TestS2EhzHalfpipeRoundTripChain`, `TestS3kAizCompleteRunTraceReplay`, and `TestS3kAiz1SkipHeadless` (all pass). Remaining chain blocker is documented in docs/status/trace-frontier-log.md: the engine's gumball exit-hold is shorter than the ROM's ~150-frame post-catch hold, so the return cursor lands short and aiz_2's fall-through frame-0 input is stale.
- Fix(s3k): S3K star-post bonus round-trip now restores the ROM-faithful checkpoint index, star-post used-state, and return position. A star-post BONUS entry zeroes `Last_star_post_hit` (ROM `Obj_StarPost` routine 8 / `loc_2D4CA`: `move.b #0,(Last_star_post_hit).w`, docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:61924), and the bonus-return path (`Load_Starpost_Settings` -> `loc_2D2C2`, :61795) never restores it, so after the round trip the checkpoint index is 0 -- NOT the triggering star post's subtype. `GameLoop.prepareBonusStageForTitleCard` previously saved `getLastCheckpointIndex()` (the subtype), mis-restoring a non-zero checkpoint on return; it now saves 0. Because the ROM keeps the star post "used" across the reload via its per-object respawn bit (`Respawn_table_keep`, :61930) independently of the zeroed index, `CheckpointState`/`RespawnState` now carry a persistent star-post activation high-water (`getStarPostActivationMark`, bumped by `saveCheckpoint`) that the star-post activation guard (`Sonic3kStarPostObjectInstance`, `loc_2CFC0` `btst #0,(a2)` :61582) consults instead of the checkpoint index; `GameLoop` captures it at bonus entry and re-establishes it on return so the returned star post -- which the player is repositioned onto -- stays used instead of re-triggering and re-saving its subtype. The bonus return also now restores the player to the STAR POST position (`Saved_X/Y_pos = x_pos/y_pos(starpost)`, `sub_2D164` :61705-61706) captured in the checkpoint state, rather than the player's live centre at touch time (which is a few px off the post), matching the recorded return frame. Drives `TestS3kMegaRunChain` past the first gumball interior's exit-boundary, checkpoint-restore, and positional-restore assertions. Verified against the six stage comparators, `TestS1GhzMazeRoundTripChain`, `TestS2EhzHalfpipeRoundTripChain`, `TestS3kAizCompleteRunTraceReplay`, `TestCheckpointStateRewind`, and the bonus lifecycle/return unit suites (all pass; `TestS3kHczCompleteRunTraceReplay` unchanged, fails identically on develop at f29095).
- Fix(s3k): Knuckles' glide now activates while star-invincible. `PlayableSpriteMovement.tryShieldAbility` applied Sonic's `Sonic_FireShield` invincibility suppression (`btst #Status_Invincible`, docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:23412-23413) to Knuckles' glide, but glide runs through the separate `Knux_Test_For_Glide` routine (sonic3k.asm:32539-32586), which has no invincibility/shield gate -- its only conditions are `double_jump_flag==0` + a jump-press edge (both already gated by the caller) and the Super/emerald transform test (handled upstream in `tryActivateSuperFromAirAbility`). The Knuckles `GLIDE` branch is now evaluated before the Sonic-only shield/super/invincibility gates, so a mid-air jump re-press activates glide even with an active invincibility timer. Sonic (insta/elemental) and Tails (flight) are unaffected -- their secondary ability is not `GLIDE`. Root-caused via a standalone AIZ replay of the `s3-knux-multibonus-ss` Knuckles run: at trace f2464 Knuckles re-presses jump after release while carrying ~1142 frames of star invincibility; the engine refused glide and stayed air-rolling (`g_speed` 0x54 vs ROM 0x400), now activates matching the ROM (`double_jump_flag` 0->1, `ground_vel` 0x400, `anim` 0x20). Verified against the six must-stay-green stage comparators, `TestS1GhzMazeRoundTripChain`, `TestS2EhzHalfpipeRoundTripChain`, `TestS3kAizCompleteRunTraceReplay`, `TestS3kMgzCompleteRunTraceReplay`, `TestPlayableSpriteMovement`, and the Knuckles unit suites (all pass; `TestS3kHczCompleteRunTraceReplay` fails identically on develop at f29095).
- Fix(s3k): Knuckles' glide→fall→slide landing now matches the ROM's `Knux_Glide_Freespace` move-then-update ordering, fixing an AIZ trajectory drift that made Knuckles miss the Giant Ride Vine grab. Four defects in `PlayableSpriteMovement`: (1) `Knux_Gliding_HitFloor` flat path (`loc_1693E`, docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:30754-30769) sets `double_jump_flag=3` and the sliding frame but NEVER clears `Status_InAir` and plays no SFX — the engine wrongly called `setAir(false)`/`playSfx` there, so the slide ran ground-flagged; (2) the glide floor probe now applies `Sonic_CheckFloor`'s odd-angle rule (`loc_F7F0`, sonic3k.asm:19884-19888: an odd tile-angle byte reads back as 0), so AIZ's flagged landing tile (0xFF) yields angle 0x00 like the ROM instead of 0xFF; (3) the slide (`Knuckles_Sliding`) and fall-from-glide (`Knuckles_Fall_From_Glide`, sonic3k.asm:30895-30943) now run `MoveSprite2` BEFORE the 0x20 slide decel / `Knux_ChgJumpDir` air-accel + `+$38` gravity, matching `Knux_Glide_Freespace` (sonic3k.asm:30675-30682) — the prior update-then-move order biased the fall by one +0x30 air-accel step per frame (~2.5px by landing); (4) `Knuckles_Move_Glide` no longer tests the jump button at its top — the release check now runs after `MoveSprite2`+collision (per `Knuckles_Glide`, sonic3k.asm:30708-30729), so a jump-release-during-glide moves at the full glide velocity before the x_vel/4 fall transition. All four paths are Knuckles-glide-only. Verified against a standalone AIZ replay of the `s3-knux-multibonus-ss` Knuckles run (the f1934 vine grab now succeeds; position matches through f2463) plus the six stage comparators, `TestS1GhzMazeRoundTripChain`, `TestS2EhzHalfpipeRoundTripChain`, `TestS3kAizCompleteRunTraceReplay`, `TestS3kMgzCompleteRunTraceReplay`, and the glide/movement unit suites (all pass; `TestS3kHczCompleteRunTraceReplay` fails identically on develop at f29095 and `TestS3kMegaRunChain` still fails on a separate, later glide-activation-from-a-spindash-roll-jump root at trace f2464, unaffected by this change).
- Fix(engine): the global oscillator (`OscillationManager`) no longer advances during the locked title-card wait phase. `GameLoop.updateTitleCardMode` now calls `LevelManager.suppressGlobalOscillationForTitleCardPass()` before each locked title-card object pass, so `advanceGlobalOscillation()` skips that frame — matching the ROM, which runs `OscillateNumDo` only inside `Level_MainLoop` (docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:5108) and never in the title-card wait loops (s2.asm:4914-4924, 5060-5066), which run `RunObjects` only. S1 mirrors this (docs/s1disasm/sonic.asm: `OscillateNumInit` 2913 and `OscillateNumDo` 3030 both sit outside `Level_TtlCardLoop` 2811-2839). Previously every locked title-card frame over-advanced the global oscillator, so oscillation-driven moving platforms (e.g. Obj18 / `ARZPlatformObjectInstance`) came back phase-offset after the title card — most visibly on a special-stage return, where the engine runs the real title card rather than the trace bootstrap that skips it (the oscillator is reset to its `OscillateNumInit` baseline by `onLevelLoad()` and must then hold at baseline until gameplay unlocks). Standalone trace-replays are unaffected because their bootstrap skips the title card; this is a live-play parity fix. Greens `TestS2EhzHalfpipeRoundTripChain` (the SS-return round trip now progresses through both star-post cycles). Verified against the six stage comparators, `TestS1GhzMazeRoundTripChain`, `TestS2Ehz1TraceReplay`, `TestS1Ghz1CompleteRunTraceReplay`, `TestS3kAizCompleteRunTraceReplay`, `TestS2CpzLevelSelectTraceReplay`, and the title-card/results unit suites (all pass; two unrelated S3K tests — `TestS3kMegaRunChain` and `TestS3kResultsScreenObjectInstance` — fail identically on develop and are not affected by this change).
- Fix(trace): `TestS1GhzMazeRoundTripChain` now drives the S1 maze special-stage interior with the recorded run's actual BK2 input instead of a neutral no-op `InputHandler`, and skips BizHawk "lag" rows the way the standalone SS trace-replay harness does, so the chain reproduces the recorded run's own ring/emerald outcome (`stage_exit`'s `rings_after`/`emeralds_after`) instead of an engine-organic (unsteered, over-ticked) one. `GameLoop`'s special-stage entry now selects `SpecialStageStartupPolicy.TRACE_ACCURATE` instead of `FAST` whenever a `PlaybackDebugManager` BK2 session is actively playing (frame-stepping the ROM's observable pre-physics hold instead of fast-forwarding it synchronously inside `initializeStage`), so a BK2-driven caller's recorded per-frame input lines up 1:1 with the special stage's own physics ticks from the very first tick — the same predicate `TraceSessionLauncher`'s own dedicated special-stage trace session already keys `TRACE_ACCURATE` on, generalized to the organic giant-ring/checkpoint-star entry path. `AbstractRunChainTest` gained an overridable `uncomparedInteriorStep` seam (default: feed every recorded BK2 row, no lag-skip) so a lane with a per-game special-stage trace format carrying a lag column can compose a lag-aware stepper.
- Fix(s2): `GameLoop.doEnterSpecialStage`'s no-policy overload now selects `SpecialStageStartupPolicy.TRACE_ACCURATE` (instead of always `FAST`) and disables the entered provider's own lag-compensation model (`setLagCompensation(0)`) whenever `PlaybackDebugManager.isSessionPlaying()` is true, mirroring `TraceSessionLauncher#enterSpecialStageTrace`'s existing pairing of the same two settings for its own dedicated special-stage trace session. `FAST` fast-forwards the ROM's observable pre-physics hold synchronously without stepping real engine frames — correct for ordinary interactive play, but it desyncs a BK2-driven caller's per-frame recorded input from the hold's own tick count, and the provider's stateless lag model (`Sonic2SpecialStageLagModel`) otherwise inserts additional synthetic skipped frames on top of whatever cadence the caller is already driving. Generalizes the fix to the organic giant-ring/checkpoint-star entry path (used both by ordinary gameplay, where no BK2 session is ever playing, and by any BK2-driven session — including `TestS2EhzHalfpipeRoundTripChain`'s chain drive — that reaches this transition). Verified against the six must-stay-green stage comparators plus `TestGameLoopSpecialStageEntryPresentation`/`TestGameLoopSpecialStageRewindBoundary`/`TestSpecialStageVisualTraceSession`/`TestTraceSessionLauncherSpecialStageEntry` (all pass unchanged).
- Test(trace): `AbstractRunChainTest` gained an overridable `uncomparedInteriorStep` seam (default `specialStageDrivenStep`, feeding every recorded BK2 row as a logical `InputHandler` override via `RecordedInputSnapshots.fromBk2`, using a segment-local row counter independent of the frozen shared `PlaybackDebugManager` cursor) so an uncompared special-stage interior is actually driven by the recorded run's own input instead of a neutral/no-op `InputHandler` for its whole duration. `TestS2EhzHalfpipeRoundTripChain` overrides the seam to additionally skip the `s2_special_stage` trace's per-row `lag` column (mirroring `S2SpecialStageReplayHarness`), matching the recorded ring/track-segment cadence byte-for-byte for the first ~1500 special-stage frames (verified via temporary diagnostic instrumentation, since removed). The lane still fails its `emeralds_after` boundary assertion; the initially-suspected `Sonic2SpecialStageManager` object-location-data defect (premature emerald-marker spawn) was DISPROVEN by follow-up instrumentation (a raw dump of the decompressed `objectLocationData` for stage 0 showed an intact ~489-byte stream) and superseded by the correct diagnosis documented on `TestS2EhzHalfpipeRoundTripChain`'s class javadoc: the committed `ss`/`ss_2` fixtures ship an empty `aux_state.jsonl.gz` (36 bytes, vs ~200KB for level segments) with zero `run_objects_end` pass records, which `SpecialStageRunObjectsPassBinder` needs to pace the ROM-object-pass-driven half-pipe; without those pass records the chain can only frame-pace the recorded BK2 input and drifts off the recorded ring cadence, so the stage is LOST rather than WON and the emerald is correctly never awarded. Fixing this requires re-recording `ss`/`ss_2` with special-stage aux state, out of scope for a comparison-only test change.
- Fix(s2): `CoconutsBadnikInstance` now defers its thrown coconut's first movement frame via `BadnikProjectileInstance.deferFirstMovementForLoadSubObjectInit()`, mirroring the identical fix already applied to `NebulaBadnikInstance`/`CluckerBadnikInstance`/`AsteronBadnikInstance`/`SpinyBadnikInstance`. ROM `Obj98_Init` (s2.asm:74665-74666) only `bra.w`s into `LoadSubObject`, which loads render/collision state and bumps `routine` 0→2 then `rts` — it never calls `Obj98_Main`/`Obj98_CoconutFall` on the frame the coconut is allocated. Without the defer the engine's freshly-thrown coconut started falling one frame early, drifting its trajectory enough to miss (or land) a player touch the ROM's one-frame-later coconut does the opposite on. Root-caused via the new `s2-ehz-halfpipe-roundtrip` chain-replay run (`TestS2EhzHalfpipeRoundTripChain`): the level-segment comparator's first (and only) mismatch, at trace frame 187 (`player_animation_id` expected `0x001A` Hurt vs actual `0x0002`, `rolling` expected `0` vs actual `1`, `x_speed`/`y_speed` off by ~1450 -- the ROM's coconut hurt-bounce the engine's one-frame-early coconut missed), is gone after this fix; the level segment now replays byte-for-byte across all 2969 recorded frames.
- Test(trace): `AbstractRunChainTest`'s drive loop now ticks `GameServices.fadeOrNull().update()` immediately before every `GameLoop.step()` (`stepEngineFrame`, replacing raw `loop::step`/`loop.step()` call sites in `stepFrames`/`waitForMode`/`waitForModeToLeave`/the two `awaitBoundary` runnables). `Engine.display()` calls `UiRenderPipeline.updateFade()` (-> `FadeManager.update()`) before `GameLoop.step()` on every real frame (Engine.java, `display()` body); `FadeManager.update()`'s only other call site in `src/main` is that same `UiRenderPipeline` method, so a headless `GameLoop`-driven test that never calls `Engine.display()` never advances a fade a boundary handler started (e.g. `GameLoop.enterSpecialStage`'s S2 checkpoint-star path always begins with `fadeManager.startFadeToWhite(() -> doEnterSpecialStage(...))`), leaving the completion callback that flips `currentGameMode` to `SPECIAL_STAGE` permanently unfired. Without this the chain drive hung at `waitForMode(..., SPECIAL_STAGE, ...)` for the full manifest-derived step cap and then threw `AssertionError("Mode never reached SPECIAL_STAGE...")`; `TestS2EhzHalfpipeRoundTripChain` now crosses the full `starpost_special` entry -> special-stage interior (advance-uncompared) -> `stage_exit` return round trip and reaches the final return-boundary assertion. `TestS1GhzMazeRoundTripChain` (a different in-progress lane) advances past the same class of hang for its own `giant_ring` entry as an incidental benefit of the shared base-class fix, confirmed by re-running it against the pre-fix version of this file via `git show HEAD:...` and comparing frontiers.
- Fix(trace): `AbstractRunChainTest`'s generalized `runChain` body previously had zero executing coverage — its only subclass pointed at two unrecorded fixture directories and both methods skipped, while the three actually-committed runs (`s3-knux-multibonus-ss`, `s1-ghz-maze-roundtrip`, `s2-ehz-halfpipe-roundtrip`) were never driven by any test. Added one `@RequiresRom` lane subclass per committed run — `TestS1GhzMazeRoundTripChain`, `TestS2EhzHalfpipeRoundTripChain`, `TestS3kMultiBonusSpecialStageRunChain` — so all three now execute end-to-end (surefire `Skipped: 0` for each); `TestS3kBonusRoundTripChain` keeps its skip-if-missing gumball/pachinko methods now that a genuinely-driven S3K lane exists alongside them. Driving the walk surfaced a real defect: `TraceRunReplayWalker.plan()` eagerly parsed every segment's `physics.csv` through `TraceFrame`'s primary-level column schema, including `special_stage` interiors whose per-game physics CSV (S1's 14-column maze schema, S2's 48-column halfpipe schema) never matches that schema and whose frames are never read anyway under SS-interior policy v1 (advance-uncompared) — crashing the S1 lane outright with `IllegalArgumentException` before any assertion ran. Added `TraceData.loadMetadataOnly` (metadata + aux events only, empty frame list) and route `plan()` through it for segments `isUncomparedInterior` flags, leaving strict physics parsing for every segment a comparator is actually built from. Also repointed the two dangling `chain-core-contract.md` citations (a file that was never committed) in `TraceRunReplayWalker`/`AbstractRunChainTest` at the extant "Decisions locked with the owner" section of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-18-multi-stage-trace-runs-design.md`. The now-executing lanes surface a separate, pre-existing content/physics gap (ground-attachment finds no floor at the S1/S2/S3K fixtures' recorded metadata start position, reproduced independently of the chain drive via the single-load `HeadlessTestFixture` path) that is out of scope for this fix and left for a dedicated trace-parity investigation.
- Fix(s3k): Knuckles' glide activation (`PlayableSpriteMovement.activateGlide`) no longer lets an incidental `setRolling(false)` side effect corrupt the player's centre Y position. ROM `Knux_Test_For_Glide` (sonic3k.asm:32560-32566) writes `y_radius`/`x_radius` directly and never touches `y_pos` — ROM's centre coordinate is unaffected by a radius change. This engine instead derives `getCentreY()` from a top-left `yPixel` plus a separate `height` field, and `setRolling(false)` (called first, to exit a roll-jump before applying glide radii) has the documented side effect of resetting `height` to the standing value (`runHeight`) whenever Knuckles was mid-roll-jump — the common case entering glide from a jump. `applyCustomRadii(10, 10)` then overwrites the radii to glide dimensions but never re-syncs `height`, so `getCentreY()` silently jumped by half the standing-vs-roll height delta *before any velocity-driven movement even ran* — an engine-internal bookkeeping artifact ROM has no equivalent of. `activateGlide()` now captures `getCentreY()` before the `setRolling`/`applyCustomRadii` calls and restores it (subpixel-preserving, matching a ROM `move.w`) afterward, making glide entry a pure radius change as ROM performs it. Root-caused via a standalone throwaway replay of `traces/s3k/runs/s3-knux-multibonus-ss/aiz/`: at trace frame 1562 this stale-height jump alone accounted for +5px of centreY, compounding with the frame's correct +5px velocity-driven move into a +10px error that desynced Knuckles' glide-entry timing for the rest of the segment (frames 1562-1601 now match trace exactly; a smaller, independent divergence starting ~frame 1721 remains open as the next frontier). `TestS3kMegaRunChain` still fails its first `starpost_bonus` boundary. Verified no regression: the six must-stay-green stage comparators plus `TestTraceRunReplayWalkerControlFlow`, `TestS3kAizCompleteRunTraceReplay` (Sonic+Tails), and the must-keep-green S3K suite (`TestS3kAiz1SkipHeadless`, `TestSonic3kLevelLoading`, `TestSonic3kBootstrapResolver`, `TestSonic3kDecodingUtils`, `TestSonic3kSpringObjectInstance`) all pass with 0 failures/skips.
- Fix: Knuckles' glide-state floor detection (`PlayableSpriteMovement.doGlideCollision`/`updateSliding`) probed only a single center point (`ObjectTerrainUtils.checkFloorDist(cx, cy + yRad)`) instead of ROM's `Sonic_CheckFloor`/`sub_11FD6` (sonic3k.asm:19839-19891, 24127-24135), which probes BOTH foot sensors (`x_pos ± x_radius`) and keeps whichever found the closer floor. A center-only probe is blind to a floor edge under one foot but not the other (e.g. a staircase lip) and lands several frames late. Added `checkGlideFloorDist(cx, cy, xRad, yRad)` (dual-sensor, picks the smaller/more-negative distance) and routed both `doGlideCollision()`'s floor check and `updateSliding()`'s floor snap/ledge-off probe through it. Root-caused via a standalone throwaway replay of `traces/s3k/runs/s3-knux-multibonus-ss/aiz/` (the prior iteration's documented frontier): at trace frame 1570 the right-foot sensor already reported floor contact (distance -4) while the center probe still reported clear air (distance +22), so the engine kept falling for 6 more frames, missed the sliding-state that ROM entered, and the resulting position drift cascaded into a ~1800px trajectory divergence by frame ~4545 near the segment's end. After the fix, frames 1560-1620 (landing, sliding, get-up, and the following jump/roll) match the trace exactly (x/y/velocities/mapping_frame all `MATCH`) aside from a pre-existing few-pixel residual drift already present before this glide event. `TestS3kMegaRunChain` still fails its first `starpost_bonus` boundary: a further Knuckles Solo AIZ divergence was newly found starting trace frame ~1934, where the recorded trace's velocity fields go to zero while position sweeps a smooth pendulum-like arc for ~65 frames (consistent with an `AizRideVineObjectInstance`-family vine grab this engine build does not trigger for this approach), diverging engine and trace by hundreds of pixels before the boundary — left as the next iteration's frontier. Verified no regression: the six must-stay-green stage comparators plus `TestTraceRunReplayWalkerControlFlow`, `TestS3kAizCompleteRunTraceReplay` (Sonic+Tails), the must-keep-green S3K suite, `TestPhysicsProfile`, `TestCollisionModel`, `TestSonic3kSuperTransformationEligibility`, and `TestKnucklesRespawnStrategy` all pass with 0 failures/skips.
- Fix: Knuckles' glide activation (`PlayableSpriteMovement.setGlideAnimation`, ROM `Knuckles_Set_Gliding_Animation`, sonic3k.asm:31560-31581) never wrote the `anim` byte, only `mapping_frame` — missing the routine's `move.w #($20<<8)|$20,anim(a0) ; and prev_anim` (sonic3k.asm:31563). A first attempt to add it via a plain `sprite.setAnimationId(0x20)` was itself stomped one frame later: `PlayableSpriteAnimation.update()` recomputes `animationId` from the scripted velocity resolver every frame *before* checking `isObjectMappingFrameControl()`, so any glide-set id needs the same `forcedAnimationId` override channel `enterFallFromGlide()`/`clearGlideAnimationState()` already use. Switched to `sprite.setForcedAnimationId(0x20)`. Found while triaging `TestS3kMegaRunChain`'s `s3-knux-multibonus-ss` AIZ segment (Knuckles solo): the recorded trace enters glide (`player_animation_id=0x20`) at frame 1562 while the engine stayed at `0x0000` for the entire glide duration. Fix confirmed via a throwaway standalone `AbstractTraceReplayTest` replay of the same segment: the animation-id-stuck-at-0 divergence at frames 1562-1601 is fully eliminated (error-group count 508→506; per-frame error count 15913→15899 over the segment). A second, independent glide-collision divergence (the engine's glide ends ~6 frames after activating, landing/falling out of glide much earlier than the ROM) remains and still blocks `TestS3kMegaRunChain`'s first `starpost_bonus` boundary — left as the next iteration's frontier. No dedicated Knuckles-glide trace fixture existed before this run, so this bug had zero prior coverage; verified no regression via the six stage comparators, `TestTraceRunReplayWalkerControlFlow`, `TestS3kAizCompleteRunTraceReplay` (Sonic+Tails), and the must-keep-green S3K suite.
- Fix(trace): `TraceReplayDriver.start()`'s unconditional post-load ground/angle/sensor snap (added the prior iteration to match `HeadlessTestFixture.Builder.build()`'s step 12) ran *after* `TraceReplaySessionBootstrap.applyStartPositionAndGroundSnap`'s S3K complete-run/bonus-stage post-title-card player-state calls (`Sonic3kLevelEventManager.applyCompleteRunSegmentPlayerStateAfterTitleCard`/`armCarryIntroHandoffAfterTitleCard`) instead of before them — the reverse of the standalone fixture-backed order, where `build()`'s step-12 snap always runs strictly before the test's own subsequent `applyStartPositionAndGroundSnap` call. Reordered `TraceReplayDriver.start()` to set the metadata start centre and snap BEFORE calling `applyStartPositionAndGroundSnap`, matching the standalone contract exactly. Confirmed via targeted instrumentation (`SpriteManager.tickPlayablePhysics`, `GameLoop.syncPlaybackInputBridge`) that `TestS3kMegaRunChain`'s boot state going into the `s3-knux-multibonus-ss`/`aiz` segment's first driven frame is now byte-identical to the trace's recorded frame -1 state (position/velocity/angle/ground all match) regardless of this ordering, so this reorder alone does not resolve that lane's remaining trace-frame-0 divergence — narrowed to originate inside `PlayableSpriteMovement.handleMovement` itself on the very first driven frame (not bootstrap, not the throwaway `HeadlessTestFixture` pre-build, not solid-object/touch collision — no object is within touch range at that frame; the `AutoSpin` loop-trigger object visible in the failure diagnostics does not run its own `update()` until after player physics for this S3K inline-solid-resolution profile). Left as the next iteration's starting point; kept because the ordering fix is independently correct regardless of that open issue.
- Fix(trace): `TraceReplayDriver.start()` (the `GameLoop`-driven live/chain replay bootstrap shared by Trace Test Mode, the headless capture tool, and `AbstractRunChainTest`) was missing the one-time unconditional post-load ground/angle/sensor establishment that `HeadlessTestFixture.Builder.build()` always performs (step 12, `GameServices.collision().resolveGroundAttachment(sprite, 14, ...)`). `TraceReplaySessionBootstrap.applyStartPositionAndGroundSnap`'s own terrain snap is intentionally gated off for S3K complete-run/bonus-stage segments (`shouldGroundSnapMetadataStartForTraceReplay`), on the assumption that a prior unconditional snap already ran — true for every `HeadlessTestFixture`-backed standalone trace test, never true for `TraceReplayDriver`. Left as the next iteration's starting point.

- Feat(trace): generalized the multi-stage run chain-replay core (`TraceRunReplayWalker`) so all three committed runs drive through one manifest-driven path with no hardcoded segment counts and no zone/route/frame carve-outs. Added pure, data-driven mappings — `boundaryEntryMode(entry_kind)` (single authority for the entry-signal switch, now consumed by `BoundaryProbe`), `returnAssertionMode(entryTransition)` (POSITIONAL_RESTORE for S2 `starpost_special`, CHECKPOINT_RESTORE for S3K `starpost_bonus`, NEXT_ACT vs RINGS_EMERALDS_ONLY split on `giant_ring` `saved_x_pos` presence), `expectedMode(segment)`, `isUncomparedInterior(segment)` (SS-interior policy v1 = advance-uncompared), and `pairBoundaries(run)` (explicit-index transition pairing, exposed pure). `awaitBoundary` now takes a manifest-derived step cap (`interSegmentStepCap` = max inter-segment BK2 offset gap + `BOUNDARY_WINDOW_FRAMES`) and throws `BoundaryStepCapExceededException` on a frozen cursor instead of hanging. Extracted the S3K bonus round-trip drive into a reusable `AbstractRunChainTest` base (manifest-driven segment walk + per-entry-kind boundary assertion helpers) that the S1/S2/S3K run lanes extend; `TestS3kBonusRoundTripChain` keeps its skip-if-missing semantics. Comparison-only throughout (boundary state is compared against organically-produced engine state, never hydrated); no behavior change to the six single-stage stage comparators.
- Fix: `PlayableSpriteAnimation`'s scripted `$FD`/`SWITCH` animation-end handler no longer eagerly snapshots `lastAnimationId` (the engine's `prev_anim` tracker) to the switched-to animation id. ROM's `Animate_Sonic`/`Animate_Tails` `$FD` handler (`loc_12698`, sonic3k.asm:24795-24801) writes only the live `anim` byte and never touches `prev_anim` or `anim_frame`; the deferred `prev_anim` sync is what let a same-frame external raw-anim rewrite (e.g. a second solid-object bounce re-publishing the pre-switch animation id later in the same frame) silently resume the interrupted script's already-past-the-end countdown for its normal remaining delay instead of restarting a fresh cycle. The engine previously called the shared `resetScriptState()` inside the `SWITCH` branch, eagerly syncing `lastAnimationId` and making the next frame's re-write look like a *fresh* animation change, which forced a full extra delay cycle and pushed the transition one frame late. Fixes `TestS3kGumballBonusTraceReplay` frame-1227 divergence (`player_animation_id` expected `0x0000` vs actual `0x0010`, from the Spring animation's own `$2F,$8E,$FD,0` auto-switch-to-Walk script colliding with a second mid-air `GumballTriangleBumperObjectInstance` bounce re-latching Spring on the exact expiry frame); the ordinary (non-interrupted) `SWITCH` case is unaffected because the caller's own `anim != lastAnimationId` check at the top of `updateScriptedAnimation` reproduces the same reset with identical timing. Trace error count drops from 10 to 0 (GREEN).
- Fix(s3k): `GumballMachineObjectInstance.GumballSpringChild` now overrides `usesPlatformObjectLandingSnap()` to `false`. ROM's gumball spring (`loc_60DAC`, sonic3k.asm:127514) calls `SolidObjectFull2_1P` (sonic3k.asm:41070), whose fresh-contact path falls through to the shared `SolidObject_cont` top-landing branch (`loc_1E154`, sonic3k.asm:41611-41637) — the same relative `playerY - distY + 3`-style placement `resolveContactInternal` already produces, not the `PlatformObject_ChkYRange` absolute `anchorY - groundHalfHeight - yRadius - 1` snap. With the override defaulting `true`, the engine's shared `applyNonUnifiedTopSolidLandingHeightOverride` re-snapped the spring's landing Y to the wrong (8px-higher) formula before `sub_22F98`'s `addq.w #8,y_pos(a1)` bounce-compression nudge applied on top, landing the player 8px too high on every gumball-bonus spring bounce. Fixes `TestS3kGumballBonusTraceReplay` frame-895 divergence (`y` expected `0x02E4` vs actual `0x02DC`) and the downstream f1015 triangle-bumper-timing cluster it fed; trace error count drops from 74 to 10 (remaining errors are animation-timing only, frontier now frame 1227).
- Fix(s3k): S3K Slots bonus stage goal-exit fade now switches the frozen player's roll animation to the Sonic roll for every character, matching the ROM's incidental `character_id` clobber. ROM `loc_4BC1E` (sonic3k.asm:98964-98972) triggers the goal fade when the rotation wind-down reaches `SStage_scalar_index_1 == $1800` and, as part of that trigger, runs `move.w #60,$38(a0)` (sonic3k.asm:98971) to seed a 60-frame countdown. `$38` is the `character_id` offset (sonic3k.constants.asm:66), so the high byte of `60` (`$003C`) overwrites `character_id` with `0`; from that frame on the shared animate dispatcher `sub_4B99E` (sonic3k.asm:98683) reads `character_id == 0` and calls `Animate_Sonic` instead of `Animate_Knuckles`/`Animate_Tails`. The object keeps its own `mappings`, so only the mapping-frame index sequence changes: the roll script becomes `AniSonic02` (`[96,97,96,98,96,99,96,9A]`, rest frame `96`) instead of `AniKnux02`/`AniTails02` (`[9A,96,9A,97,9A,98,9A,99]`, rest frame `9A`). `S3kSlotBonusStageRuntime` now swaps the slot player's ROLL/ROLL2 scripts to the Sonic-half scripts (parsed from ROM) into an isolated animation-set copy when the exit fade begins, leaving `anim_frame`/timer in phase. Advances `TestS3kSlotsBonusTraceReplay` from frame 967 to GREEN (5 to 0 errors).
- Fix(s3k): S3K Slots bonus stage camera now keeps tracking the player through the goal-exit sequence instead of freezing on the last pre-goal frame. ROM's per-frame `Obj_Sonic_RotatingSlotBonus` dispatch always falls through to the shared tail `loc_4B97C` (Animate, DPLC, `sub_4BBF4` camera track, Draw_Sprite) no matter which `routine(a0)` branch ran — including the goal-exit handler `loc_4BC1E` (sonic3k.asm:98964-99005) and its self-modified palette-fade successor `loc_4BC54`, which itself ends with `bra.w loc_4B97C`. `S3kSlotBonusStageRuntime.update()`'s early-return for the exiting state skipped `updateCamera()` entirely, leaving the camera stuck at whatever value it held the frame before the goal fired. Camera position is now recomputed every exit-sequence frame (numerically stable once the player's own position freezes, matching ROM). Advances `TestS3kSlotsBonusTraceReplay` from frame 868 to frame 967 (15 to 5 errors).
- Fix(s3k): S3K Slots bonus stage goal-exit no longer reports a fabricated airborne/wrong-routine player state. ROM's goal-tile dispatch branch `loc_4BED0` (sonic3k.asm:99247-99253) does nothing but `addq.b #2,routine(a0)` (2->4) and play `sfx_Goal` — it never touches `status(a0)`; by the time it runs, `sub_4BCB0` (air gravity, called earlier the same frame) has already cleared `Status_InAir` for whichever axis the goal tile collided on, since touching any solid special tile guarantees a same-frame `bclr #Status_InAir,status(a0)` (sonic3k.asm:99032/99050). `S3kSlotPlayerRuntime.startGoalExit()` unconditionally forced `player.setAir(true)`, overwriting that already-correct grounded state for the whole frozen goal-exit sequence, and nothing exposed ROM's `routine(a0)` 2->4 transition at all (the generic `TraceCharacterState.routineFromSprite` heuristic only derives 2/4/6 from hurt/dead/CPU-state, which doesn't apply to this custom ROM object reusing the same byte offset for its own state machine). Added `AbstractPlayableSprite.objectRoutineOverride` (consulted first by `routineFromSprite`) so a player object whose dispatch has been swapped for a custom ROM object can report its own raw `routine(a0)` value, and latch it to 4 on goal-exit start instead of forcing air. Advances `TestS3kSlotsBonusTraceReplay` from frame 868 (30 errors) with the routine/air/status_byte fields now matching (camera_x/y fixed separately, see entry above).
- Fix(s3k): S3K Slots bonus stage reel-wall flash now runs at the ROM's 2-frame-per-colour-frame cadence instead of 1. ROM `loc_4B65A` (sonic3k.asm:98499-98515) advances one `byte_4B688` colour frame only when its per-slot countdown `subq.b #1,2(a0)` goes negative and reloads it with `move.b #1,2(a0)` (a reset+1 = 2-tick period), giving a ~48-frame flash over the 24 colour frames; the engine's `SLOT_WALL_COLOR_DELAY=1` flashed twice as fast. The flash keeps a hit reel cell a plain-solid (0x0D-0x0F) until it restores the advanced tile, so a repeatedly-hit reel wall re-advances 1->2->3->4 (tile 4 = goal, `loc_4BED0`/`loc_4BF30`) at the flash cadence; at 2x speed cell 188 turned into a goal ~72 frames early and fired a spurious goal-exit that froze the player and camera. Advances `TestS3kSlotsBonusTraceReplay` from frame 809 to frame 868 (113 to 30 errors).
- Fix(s3k): S3K Slots bonus stage bumper launch now advances the player's position on the firing frame instead of lagging one frame — the "distinct downstream root" flagged in the entry below. ROM `Obj_Sonic_RotatingSlotBonus`'s movement path (`loc_4BA98`, sonic3k.asm:98776-98780) runs `sub_4BDCA` (ring pickup) and `sub_4BE3A` (tile dispatch — whose bumper branch `loc_4BE5A`, sonic3k.asm:99213-99239, overwrites `x_vel`/`y_vel` with the `GetArcTan`-derived `0x700` launch velocity) *before* `jsr MoveSprite2` folds the updated velocity into `x_pos`/`y_pos`, so a bumper hit moves the player by the launch velocity on the same frame it fires. The engine ran the tile dispatch in `S3kSlotBonusStageRuntime.update()`, which fires *after* the sprite manager already ticked the player's `applyVelocityStep` (the `MoveSprite2` equivalent) with the pre-dispatch collision-zeroed velocity, so the launch reached position only one frame later (frame 446: engine `y_pos`=0x0333.B500 = ROM's frame-445 value; ROM=0x032C.BC00 = frame-445 + launch `y_vel`<<8; the +0x6F900 gap equals exactly one launch-velocity step). Moved ring pickup + tile dispatch (+ the spike/slot-wall throttle bleed-down) into a pre-move hook `S3kSlotPlayerRuntime.tick` invokes between air-gravity collision and the velocity step — the exact ROM `sub_4BDCA`/`sub_4BE3A`-before-`MoveSprite2` seam; object-controlled (cage grab, `loc_4BA80`) and debug frames skip that movement branch and keep the throttle/slot-wall hygiene via an `update()` fallback (in-tick jumps like frame 429's B-button launch were already applied before the velocity step, which is why only bumpers lagged). Advances `TestS3kSlotsBonusTraceReplay` from frame 446 to frame 809 (236 to 113 errors).
- Fix(s3k): S3K Slots bonus stage bumper-tile launch direction no longer reconstructs the wrong grid column. `S3kSlotCollisionSystem.tileResponseAnchorX/Y` recovered the collided tile's row/col from the stored `$32(a0)`-equivalent pointer by adding 1 to the expanded layout index, but ROM sub_4BE3A's `subi.l #-$CFFF,d1` (sonic3k.asm:99214-99215) already cancels the post-increment `+1` baked into sub_4BDA2's stored pointer (`TABLE=$3000`; `$3000+$CFFF+1==$10000`, so the low-word reconstruction is exactly the hit index, not index+1) -- the extra `+1` shifted the reconstructed bumper center one column right of the tile that actually triggered it, producing the correct `0x700` launch magnitude but the wrong direction (a diagonal launch instead of ROM's near-vertical one). Also hardened `S3kSlotCollisionSystem.checkCollision` to scan all four corners unconditionally and let the last special (1-6) corner found win, instead of returning on the first solid corner, matching ROM sub_4BD5A's four unconditional `sub_4BDA2` calls where a plain-solid/empty corner never clears an earlier special-tile latch. Fixes `TestS3kSlotsBonusTraceReplay`'s frame-446 y_speed divergence (expected=-0x6F9, actual=-0x52B, confirmed by an exact numeric match once the `+1` is removed); a distinct downstream root (the tile-dispatch velocity override applies one frame later than ROM's same-frame `MoveSprite2`, since dispatch runs in `S3kSlotBonusStageRuntime.update()` after the player's own per-frame `applyVelocityStep` already folded the pre-dispatch velocity into position) now surfaces as the frame-446 first error instead.
- Fix(s3k): `S3kSlotRingRewardObjectInstance` now reports its cage active-reward-count decrement (`S3kSlotStageController.onRewardExpired`) at the exact ring-grant instant instead of after its cosmetic sparkle animation finishes, and `S3kSlotBonusCageObjectInstance.updateRelease` now assigns the release-launch velocity as `x_speed=sin(angle)*4` / `y_speed=cos(angle)*4` instead of the swapped `cos`-to-x/`sin`-to-y pairing. - Fix(s3k): `S3kSlotBonusStageRuntime.primeVIntRunCountForReplay` now primes its `V_int_run_count` proxy base from the trace's own `TraceData.initialVblankCounter()` instead of a live `ObjectManager.vblaCounter` read taken at priming time. `TraceReplaySessionBootstrap.applyBonusStageEntry` (which calls the primer) runs from `afterFixtureBuild`, which fires *before* `TraceReplaySessionBootstrap.applyBootstrap` seeds `ObjectManager.vblaCounter` via `initVblaCounter(trace.initialVblankCounter() - objectPreludeFrames - 1)`, so the old live read captured the pre-seed counter (0 on the freshly loaded bonus-zone level) instead of the trace's real starting value (1024 for `bonus_slots`), baking a constant +1024 (bit 10) error into every later `globalVIntRunCounter()` read. Most `Slots_CycleOptions` (sonic3k.asm:99614-99946) consumers only read the low byte of `V_int_run_count` (`move.b (V_int_run_count+3).w,d0`, bits 0-7), which a bit-10 error left untouched -- why the first spin's reel *symbols* already matched (044cf51fd) -- but it corrupted the bit-8-and-up consumers: the reel-2 velocity offset (`move.b (V_int_run_count+2).w,d0`, sonic3k.asm:99690-99694) and the random-target draw's word addend (`add.w (V_int_run_count+2).w,d0`, sonic3k.asm:99722), which feed the DECELERATE/LOCK_REELS reel-search timing. Advances `TestS3kSlotsBonusTraceReplay`'s frame-301 rings divergence (engine's first ring grant at local frame 275+26=301 vs ROM's recorded 282+26=308) to frame 307 (182 to 173 errors); a residual 1-frame gap remains open for a follow-up root.
