- **S1 end-of-act card models ROM `Got_ChkPLC`'s title-card PLC-decompression wait, fixing the SBZ2 right-boundary-scroll timing — SBZ2 GREEN (11@f8941 -> 0 errors, 17th S1 green):** ROM `GotThroughCard` routine 0 (`Got_ChkPLC`, docs/s1disasm/_incObj/3A Got Through Card.asm) idles (`tst.l (v_plc_buffer); beq Got_Main; rts`) until the title-card PLC finishes decompressing before `Got_Main` builds the card elements and the slide-in begins. The title-card art `Nem_TitleCard` (sonic.asm @ $39204; `PLC_TitleCard` in Pattern Load Cues.asm) is 128 tiles (artnem/Title Cards.nem header word $8080, low 15 bits = $80), and the gameplay VBlank decompresses 3 Nemesis tiles/frame (`ProcessPLC_3Tiles`, called from `VBlank_UpdateScreen` for `id_VBlank_Levels`), so the card holds for `ceil(128/3) = 43` frames. The engine's PLC pipeline loads art instantly, so `Sonic1ResultsScreenObjectInstance` started its slide-in immediately, running the whole end-of-act sequence (slide-in 68 + pre-tally 180 + tally + post-tally 180 + SBZ2 slide-out 34) 43 frames early. In SBZ2 that sequence ends with the `Got_SBZ2_Boundary` (`loc_C766`) right-camera-boundary scroll (`addq.w #2,(v_limitright2)` to $2100), which un-clamps `Sonic_LevelBound` and lets the chased player advance; firing it 43 frames early scrolled the camera (and released the player from the $1E40 right boundary) at f8941 instead of ROM's f8984. Fix: the results object now models the `Got_ChkPLC` PLC-decompression delay (`PLC_DECOMPRESS_FRAMES = ceil(TITLE_CARD_TILE_COUNT/PLC_TILES_PER_FRAME) = 43`) as a routine-0 idle before the slide-in, rendering nothing while it waits (ROM has not built the elements yet). A BizHawk-free trace decode confirmed the engine's internal results timing (68/180/21/180/34) was already byte-faithful and the spawn frame (signpost touch f8333 + 123-frame spin = card f8457) matched ROM exactly — the only missing piece was the PLC wait. This is game-wide S1 act-end behaviour (routine 0 of every `GotThroughCard`), not an SBZ2 carve-out; SBZ2 is simply where the resulting boundary-scroll cadence is observed frame-by-frame. Cross-game safe / no regression: the full S1 `*TraceReplay` sweep, S2 EHZ1, `TestRewindCoverageGuard`, and `TestArchitecturalSourceGuard` stay green except the pre-existing reds MZ2 (1116@f2823) and SLZ3 (22@f12712), both byte-identical pre/post fix. docs/s1disasm/_incObj/3A Got Through Card.asm (Got_ChkPLC/Got_Main/Got_SBZ2_Boundary); docs/s1disasm/_inc/Pattern Load Cues.asm (PLC_TitleCard); docs/s1disasm/sonic.asm (ProcessPLC_3Tiles, VBlank_UpdateScreen, RunPLC).
- **S1 SLZ boss spikeball still explodes on contact with the ALREADY-defeated boss, so a ball launched just after the killing hit no longer arcs back down and spuriously hurts the player (SLZ3 f12712 -> f12784, 22 -> 4 errors):** ROM `BossSpikeball_HitBoss` (loc_18EAA/loc_18EC0, docs/s1disasm/_incObj/`7A, 7B Boss - SLZ Main and Spike Balls.asm`:665-734) scans for `id_BossStarLight` and tests the ball/boss hitbox overlap WITHOUT ever checking the boss's defeated flag (`obStatus` bit 7) or its `obColType`; on overlap it advances the ball to `BossSpikeball_Explode` (`addq.b #2,obRoutine`), clears `obSubtype`, clears the boss `obColType`, and decrements `obBossHits` (which simply runs negative via `bne loc_18F38` when the boss is already dead). The boss main object persists at its arena position through the Explode/Recover phases until it escapes, so a flying ball still detonates against it post-defeat. The engine gated the collision check on `!boss.getState().defeated`, so a spikeball the player launched on the seesaw immediately after the final hit sailed straight past the defeated boss, reached its apex, descended, and hit the standing player's `col_hurt` box — knocking him into `Sonic_Hurt` (y_speed -0400, x_speed +0200, a ring lost, airborne) where ROM has him standing still (y_speed 0) and the ball already exploded against the boss (~f12646). Fix: `Sonic1SLZBossSpikeball.updateFlying` drops the `!defeated` guard (still requires the boss object to exist), and calls `onSpikeballHit()` (a no-op once `state.defeated`, matching ROM's harmless negative `obBossHits` subq) while clearing the ball velocity only on the hit that actually causes defeat (`!wasDefeated && nowDefeated`, the ROM `else` branch `bset #7 / clr obVelX / clr obVelY`); already-defeated hits keep velocity for the final pre-explosion physics step (loc_18F38). SLZ-boss-only (S1-only class), comparison-only, no zone/route/frame carve-out. SLZ3 advances f12712 -> f12784 (22 -> 4 errors; new frontier is the shared boss-escape camera-boundary-unlock-by-2 timing root, identical to SBZ2 f8941, not boss-specific); all 16 S1 trace greens (incl. SLZ1/SLZ2), S2 EHZ1, `TestRewindCoverageGuard`, and `TestArchitecturalSourceGuard` stay green (other S1 reds MZ2 f2823 / SBZ2 f8941 byte-identical pre/post).
- **Object placement spawns within a chunk in ROM layout-table order, not strict X order, fixing the SBZ2 co-located ObjPosLoad slot wall (SBZ2 14 -> 11 errors, frontier f6839 -> f8941):** `AbstractPlacementManager` and `Sonic1ObjectPlacement` now sort the spawn list by chunk-aligned X (`x & 0xFF80`) with a *stable* sort, so objects in the same 0x80 spawn column keep their ROM layout-table order. ROM `ObjPosLoad` (S1, docs/s1disasm/_inc/ObjPosLoad.asm) and `ObjectsManager_Main` (S2/S3K) window objects against chunk-aligned spawn-window edges (`v_opl_screen & $FF80` +/- $80/$280), so every object inside one 0x80 column always loads in the same pass, and the forward/backward scans walk the layout table in stored order (`a0 += 6`/`a0 -= 6`); `FindFreeObj` then hands out ascending free slots in that walk order. A BizHawk PC-execute probe (`tools/bizhawk/s1_sbz2_slot_probe.lua`; PCs 0xE10E/0xE12E/0xE14A/0xDCCE) proved that at SBZ2 f6798 ROM spawns chunk 0x1580 in stored order with `0x72@0x1594` BEFORE the two `@0x1590` objects (a within-chunk X inversion), placing the swing platform (Obj0x15) at slot 0x43 and the Bomb (Obj0x5F) at slot 0x44. The engine's strict full-X sort moved `0x72@0x1594` after the `@0x1590` pair, so the Bomb became the engine's 2nd column allocation (slot 0x43) instead of ROM's 3rd (0x44) — the `obj_s44_slot` divergence at f6839. The chunk-granular stable sort is identical to full-X for layout tables already X-sorted within each chunk (S2/S3K), and the window/`lowerBound` math uses chunk-aligned edges so within-chunk X wiggle never affects a boundary decision. Cross-game safe: all 16 S1 trace greens held, S2 EHZ1 + S3K keep-green (`TestS3kAiz1SkipHeadless`/`TestSonic3kLevelLoading`/`TestSonic3kBootstrapResolver`/`TestSonic3kDecodingUtils`) + `TestRewindCoverageGuard` + `TestArchitecturalSourceGuard` passed, and the other S1 reds are byte-identical pre/post fix (MZ2 1116@f2823, SLZ3 65@f11325). SBZ2 advances 14@f6839 -> 11@f8941 (new frontier is a distinct SBZ stomper-door Obj0x6B ride root, not placement). docs/s1disasm/_inc/ObjPosLoad.asm (OPL_Main/OPL_MovedRight/OPL_MovedLeft); docs/s1disasm/_incObj/sub FindFreeObj.asm.
- **S1 SLZ boss spikeball now explodes IN PLACE (keeping its slot + seesaw link) instead of destroy+spawn-separate, fixing the boss drop-cadence phase-lag — SLZ3 advanced f11325 -> f12712 (65 -> 22 errors):** ROM `BossSpikeball_Explode` does `move.b #id_Explosion,obID(a0)` (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/`7A, 7B Boss - SLZ Main and Spike Balls.asm`:833-864), an in-place obID change, so a self-destructed/landed spikeball BECOMES the Obj3F explosion in its own object slot and KEEPS its `objoff_3C` (= linked seesaw address) for the whole ~41-frame explosion life. The released-ROM FixBugs=0 `BSLZ_MakeBall .checkForBall` duplicate-scan is a raw 4-byte `objoff_3C` compare over slots 1..63, so it still matches that lingering explosion and ABORTS a fresh drop on the same seesaw. The engine had been destroying the spikeball and spawning a separate `ExplosionObjectInstance`, dropping the seesaw link, so its `targetSeesawHasPendingBall` missed it and the boss dropped where ROM aborts — each wrongly-made drop adds a ~40-frame `BSLZ_MakeBall` countdown pause (no `BossMove` during the countdown), compounding to a ~96px boss phase-lag that missed the seesaw spring launching the player at f11325. Fix: `Sonic1SLZBossSpikeball.updateExploding` keeps the ball alive in its slot as the Obj3F explosion (collision off, renders via the shared explosion renderer, S1 timing init/reload=7, deletes at frame 5, retains its seesaw) so the boss duplicate-scan sees it exactly as ROM does. Drop/abort cadence verified against BizHawk RAM ground truth: matches ROM for 25 consecutive events then now also aborts at vfc 10938 and realigns through vfc 11232+. SLZ-boss-only (S1-only class); SLZ1/SLZ2/S2-EHZ1/S3K must-keeps and the rewind/architecture guards stay green.
- **S1 MZ boss now defers its defeat-routine dispatch by one frame like the GHZ/SYZ bosses, so the escape camera boundary opens on the ROM frame — MZ3 GREEN (f16868 -> 0 errors):** `Sonic1MZBossInstance` was missing the `defeatDeferralAppliesToThisBoss()` override that `Sonic1GHZBossInstance` and `Sonic1SYZBossInstance` already carry. ROM `BMZ_Defeated` (loc_18392, docs/s1disasm/_incObj/`73, 74 Boss - MZ Main and Fire.asm`:146-153) selects `ob2ndRout=4` (BMZ_Explode), sets the 180-frame timer, clears `obVelX`, and `rts` WITHOUT falling through to the explode action; `BMZ_ShipMain` re-reads `ob2ndRout` at the top each frame, so the explode countdown's first `subq.w #1` lands the frame AFTER the killing hit. The engine selects the defeat routine during the touch-response pass that runs BEFORE the boss's own `update()`, so without the one-frame deferral `updateDefeatWait()` decremented the timer on the hit frame — shifting the entire explode(181) + recover-fall(29) + rise(56) chain one executed frame early, so `BMZ_Escape`'s `addq.w #2,(v_limitright2)` opened the right camera boundary one frame early (engine camera_x 0x1802 vs ROM 0x1800 at f16868, leading through f17043). A BizHawk PC-probe (REV01 s1.gen; hooks at BMZ_Recover 0x18CDC / BMZ_Escape 0x18D32, v_limitright2 @0xFFF72A) proved the boss internal timeline is byte-identical to ROM (the recover-fall ends via `cmpi.w #boss_mz_y+$60,obBossY` at the same relative frame, escape triggers at the same +56 offset) — only the start frame was off-by-one. Fix: override `defeatDeferralAppliesToThisBoss()` to return `true`, with the same ROM-cited justification as the GHZ/SYZ overrides; MZ-boss-only (Obj0x73), comparison-only, cross-game safe, no zone/route/frame carve-out. MZ3 advances f16868 -> GREEN (16th S1 green); the focused `TestS1*CompleteRunTraceReplay` + `TestS2Ehz1CompleteRunTraceReplay` + `TestRewindCoverageGuard` + `TestArchitecturalSourceGuard` sweep stays green except the pre-existing reds MZ2 f2823, SBZ2 f6839, SLZ3 f11325 (verified byte-identical first-error frames with the fix stashed).
- **S1 SBZ slot-cadence fidelity: bomb-fuse off-by-one, FindNextFreeObj RAM-full skip, swing-chain en-masse parent delete, dormant ground-saw out_of_range skip (SBZ2 21 -> 14 errors, first slot divergence f1595 -> f6408):** Four ROM-cited object-lifecycle fixes that drift the engine's OST occupancy away from the recorded ROM and ultimately cause the SBZ2 `obj_s44_slot` cascade. (1) **Walking Bomb (Obj0x5F) fuse timer.** `Bom_Action_Waiting`/`Bom_Action_Walking` decrement `bom_time` on the SAME frame after `Bom_CheckStartFuse` sets it to 143 (`subq.w #1,bom_time(a0)`; docs/s1disasm/_incObj/5F Badnik - Walking Bomb.asm:56-79), so the 143-frame fuse expires at T+143. The engine's `checkSonic` returned before that tick (T+144), exploding the bomb -> in-place id_Explosion one frame late and freeing the explosion slot one frame late (SBZ2 f1595). (2) **Shrapnel/fuse FindNextFreeObj skip.** ROM `Bom_BurnFuseAndExplode`/`Bom_CheckStartFuse` skip a shrapnel/fuse child when `FindNextFreeObj` finds no free slot AFTER the parent (`bne.s .nextShrapnel`/`.return`; Walking Bomb.asm:111-112,191-192; sub FindFreeObj.asm:32-50). The engine's `spawnFreeChild` fell back to a lowest-free `FindFreeObj` slot, fabricating shrapnel ROM never made when four fuses expired the same frame with only six high slots free (SBZ2 f1596). It now allocates `allocateSlotAfter` up front and skips the piece on -1. (3) **Swing platform (Obj0x15) en-masse chain deletion.** ROM chain links run `Swing_Display` (no out_of_range) and are deleted only by the parent's `Swing_ChkDel -> Swing_DelAll` at the parent's own ExecuteObjects slot (Swinging Platforms.asm:247-269). The engine's per-link out_of_range self-deleted lower-slot links BEFORE a higher-slot sibling chain's makechain ran the same frame, freeing slots ROM still held (SBZ2 f2103). The links are now persistent (`isPersistent` mirrors SpikedBallChain $57 ChainChild) and the parent's `onUnload` does the en-masse `DeleteChild`; the parent's `getOutOfRangeReferenceX` now returns `swing_origX` (the pivot), matching `Swing_ChkDel`. (4) **Dormant ground saw (Obj0x6A) out_of_range skip.** A not-yet-appeared ground saw that fails its player-X proximity test — or activates — runs `addq.l #4,sp`, popping `Saw_Action`'s return address and SKIPPING the trailing `out_of_range.s .delete` (6A SBZ Saws and Pizza Cutters.asm:127-131,150-152,165-170); only the player-Y failure path falls through to out_of_range. The engine ran out_of_range unconditionally, deleting a dormant saw ROM kept (SBZ2 f3085). A one-frame skip flag set by the X-fail/activation paths now models the pop. These advance the SBZ2 first slot-occupancy divergence f1595 -> f6408 and drop SBZ2 errors 21 -> 14; the SBZ2 `obj_s44_slot` first-error frame stays f6839 (residual is a co-located ObjPosLoad spawn-cadence wall at f6408 — a saw co-located with a conveyor at 0x1380,0x00D0 that the engine spawns one frame late at a higher slot; see TRACE_FRONTIER_LOG). Zero regression: all S1 trace greens (incl. GHZ/MZ1/SLZ1/SLZ2/SBZ1/SBZ3 swing-platform + SLZ/SBZ bomb/saw routes), S2 EHZ1, `TestRewindCoverageGuard`, and `TestArchitecturalSourceGuard` stay green; MZ2 f2823 / MZ3 f16868 / SLZ3 f11325 byte-identical.
- **MZ boss falling fireball now drops on its spawn frame, so it hurts the player on time (MZ3 f16303 -> f16868):** ROM `BossFire_Main` `loc_1870A` (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/`73, 74 Boss - MZ Main and Fire.asm`:537-557) sets the drop counter + queues the fireball sfx and then has no `rts`/branch — it falls straight through into `BossFire_Action`, so the spawn frame also runs one `BossFire_Drop` tick. `Sonic1BossFireInstance.updateInit` returned after the sfx instead, deferring the first drop a frame. The falling `BossFire` (Obj0x74) therefore sat ~4px high (engine y 0294 vs ROM 0298) at the contact frame and missed the player, so the engine kept him grounded and decelerating (x_speed -0054) where ROM `Sonic_Hurt`s him (air 0->1, x_speed -0200, y_speed -0400, 3 rings lost). The init now sets `routine=ROUTINE_ACTION` and runs `updateAction()` in the same frame to replicate the ROM fall-through (MZ3-only; `BossFire` spawns only in the MZ boss arena). MZ3 advances f16303 (32 errors) -> f16868 (16 errors, new separate MZ-boss-escape camera-boundary-timing frontier); all 15 S1 greens, S2 EHZ1, the rewind coverage guard, and the architectural source guard stay green.
- **S1 SBZ Teleporter (Obj0x72) preserves the player's sub-pixel fraction through every movement phase (SBZ2 f2920 -> f6839):** The SBZ teleporter takes object control of the player (`f_playerctrl=$81`) and flings him along a waypoint path. ROM `Tele_Bump` (`move.w d2,obY(a1)`), the `Tele_Bend` waypoint snap (`move.w objoff_36/38,obX/obY(a1)`), the release (`andi.w #$7FF,obY(a1)`), and the per-frame travel step `loc_167DA` (`move.l obX(a1); ... add.l obVelX<<8,obX`) all write only the x_pos/y_pos PIXEL words and accumulate position via the standard 16.16 fixed-point add, leaving the 16-bit x_sub/y_sub intact (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/72 SBZ Teleporter.asm:90-92,110-111,130-141,146). `Sonic1TeleporterObjectInstance` instead zeroed the sub-pixel via `setCentreX/Y` in the rise/snap/release and used a separate 16.8 accumulator seeded from `playerX << 8` (discarding the carried sub-pixel) for the travel move. The player runs into the teleporter carrying x_sub=0x8E/y_sub=0x2E; ROM preserves them, so when the first waypoint velocity (velX=-0x666) is applied the result is $118E.28, while the engine — having dropped the fraction — landed at $118D.00 (1px short). Fix: rise/snap/release now use `NativePositionOps.writeX/YPosPreserveSubpixel`, and the travel step uses the sprite's existing `AbstractSprite.move()` (the exact ROM 16.16 `loc_167DA` add); the redundant `posX_16_8`/`posY_16_8` accumulators were removed. Object-local to the S1 SBZ teleporter (S1-only, SBZ-only); no zone/route/frame carve-out. SBZ2 advances f2920 (501 errors) -> f6839 (21 errors; new separate `obj_s44_slot` slot-cadence frontier, player physics now byte-identical incl. `sub=(7200,0900)`); all 15 S1 greens, S2 EHZ1, the S3K must-keeps, `TestRewindCoverageGuard`, and `TestArchitecturalSourceGuard` stay green (other S1 reds MZ2 f2823 / MZ3 f16303 / SLZ3 f11325 byte-identical).
- **The eased vertical bottom camera boundary no longer clamps back to its target after each ease step (MZ3 f15324 -> f16303):** ROM `DynamicLevelEvents` (docs/s1disasm/_inc/DynamicLevelEvents.asm:5-49) and the byte-identical S2 `RunDynamicLevelEvents` (docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:20329-20364) move `Camera_Max_Y_pos`/`v_limitbtm2` toward its target by +/-2px (or +8 airborne) with **no clamp to the target on either path**. On the move-up (decreasing) path, once `Camera_Y` has passed the target the ROM snaps `v_limitbtm2 = (Camera_Y & $FFFE) - 2` — one step *below* the target — and leaves it there, letting it converge the next frame via the +2 down path. `Camera.updateBoundaryEasing()` had an extra `(diff < 0 && maxY < target)` overshoot clamp that overrode this deliberate below-target snap, leaving the boundary 2px low. At MZ3 f15323 the ROM camera reached 0211 (still below the eased boundary 06E0), snapping `v_limitbtm2` to 020E; f15324 `ScrollVertical` then clamps the camera to 020E, but the engine clamped to its target 0210 (a 2px camera_y miss). Removing the non-ROM clamp makes both the snap and the un-snapped even-step ease converge exactly as ROM. MZ3 advances f15324 (33 errors) -> f16303 (32 errors, new separate player x_speed frontier); all 15 S1 greens, S2 EHZ1, `TestCamera`, and the rewind coverage guard stay green, and the S3K AIZ/ICZ complete-run frontiers are unchanged (baseline-verified).
- **Collected scattered ("lost") rings now run their sparkle/delete countdown on the executed-frame counter instead of the VBlank counter, deleting their SST slot on the ROM-exact frame (SBZ2 f2323 -> f2920):** ROM `Obj37` `RLoss_Sparkle`/`RLoss_Delete` advances `AnimateSprite` once per `ExecuteObjects` pass (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/25, 37 Rings.asm:367-374; Ani_Ring delay byte 5 -> 4 frames x 6 + afRoutine), so a collected lost ring's slot frees ~`sparkleFrameCount*sparkleDelay+1` *executed* frames after collection. The engine's `LostRingObjectInstance.update` was driven by the VBlank counter the object loop passes in (`ObjectManager.java:667`), which also ticks on lag frames (`ObjectManager.java:2217`), so a collected lost ring deleted its slot early by the number of lag frames during its sparkle. In SBZ2 a lost ring (ROM slot 113) collected at f2251 deleted at f2276 (21 executed frames) instead of ROM's f2281 (25 executed frames); the early-freed slot let the `@0E80` Spiked-Ball-on-Chain (Obj0x15) win its `FindFreeObj` allocation at the f2280 camera-chunk move, while ROM's full 96/96 SST stalled that `OPL_MakeItem` spawn until the next chunk move at f2306. The early swing chain links occupied low slots 32/33/36/44 — the slot ROM gives the `@0E80` `-2` conveyor (Obj0x68) at f2306 — pushing the conveyor to a high slot so ascending `ExecuteObjects` ran the `+2` belt before the `-2` belt and netted the player 2px short (f2323 x 0x0DFE vs 0x0E00). Fix: `LostRingObjectInstance` times the collected-sparkle delete on `ObjectManager.getFrameCounter()` (executed frames, matching the placed-ring Obj25 path `Sonic1RingInstance` -> `RingManager.isCollectedAndSparkleDone`); the per-ring floor-check cadence still uses `v_vbla_byte` via `resolveVblaCounter()`. Cross-game shared (`level.rings`), object-agnostic, no zone/route/frame carve-out. SBZ2 advances f2323 (609 errors) -> f2920 (501 errors, new separate object-controlled x frontier); MZ2/MZ3/SLZ3 frontiers byte-identical, all 15 S1 greens + S2 EHZ1 + S3K must-keeps + rewind coverage guard stay green.
- **A mid-loop-spawned child placed into a slot at or below its parent's current execution slot stays touch-ineligible until the frame after its first own execution (MZ3 f14132 -> f15324):** ROM `ReactToItem` gates each object on `tst.b obRender(a1) / bpl.s .next` (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/sub ReactToItem.asm:50-51), and `obRender` bit 7 is set by `DisplaySprite` during the object's own `ExecuteObjects` pass. A child dropped by FindFreeObj into a slot already passed in this frame's slot-ordered loop (e.g. a horizontal MZ Lava Ball, Obj0x14 at slot 39, spawned by its Lava Ball Maker, Obj0x13 at slot 52) does not run/display until the next frame, so it cannot be touched until the frame after that first execution. The engine only suppressed touch for the same-frame (higher-slot) child case, leaving the lower-slot child touch-eligible one frame too early — so the lava ball hurt the rolling player at MZ3 f14132 (rings 25->0, hurt bounce x_speed 0x0200 / y_speed -0x0400) one frame before ROM (which hurts at f14133). `ObjectManager.addDynamicObjectInternal` now marks such a child `awaitingFirstTouchExecution`; `AbstractObjectInstance.isOnScreenForTouch()` (the engine's `obRender` bit-7 equivalent) returns false while the flag is set, and `executeObjectWithSolidContext` clears it after the object's first `update()`. Generic ROM-state gate (child slot vs parent exec slot), object-agnostic, no zone/route/frame carve-out. MZ3 advances f14132 (447 errors) -> f15324 (33 errors, new separate camera_y frontier); all 15 S1 greens (incl MZ1), S2 EHZ1, and the rewind coverage guard stay green.
- **S1 Walking Bomb (Obj0x5F) body despawns via the exact ROM out_of_range macro, completing the bomb-lifecycle RememberState consistency:** `Sonic1BombBadnikInstance.isPersistent()` now uses `isInRange()` (the chunk-aligned 640px `out_of_range` macro) instead of the approximate symmetric `isOnScreenX(160)`, matching `Bom_Action`'s `bra.w RememberState` tail (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/5F Badnik - Walking Bomb.asm:49; Macros.asm:273-289) and the fuse child, which already used `isInRange()`. Cross-game safe (bomb code shared with SLZ green zones). SBZ2 frontier unchanged at f2323; all S1 greens (incl. SLZ1/SLZ2/SBZ1/SBZ3 walking-bomb routes), S2 EHZ1, and TestRewindCoverageGuard stay green (only the 4 known S1 reds fail).
- **S1 MZ lava wall Obj4E clears its respawn counter at ROM timing without rematerializing early:** `Sonic1LavaWallObjectInstance` now mirrors Obj4E `.startDelete`: it clears `v_objstate` bit 7 immediately (`bclr #7,2(a2,d0.w)`) and then switches to routine 8 for the later `DeleteObject` tail. The S1 counter placement layer now exposes a scoped helper that clears the counter and marks the spawn dormant until ObjPosLoad's cursor naturally reprocesses the entry, preventing a same-frame duplicate load while preserving the ROM-visible bit state. Added coverage for immediate bit clear, dormant cadence, trail-slot same-pass deletion, and the MZ lava-wall art remap tile range. Verification for this fix showed no MZ frontier regression relative to its baseline: MZ2 stayed at f2823 and MZ3 stayed at f14132; current develop later advances MZ3 to f15324 via the mid-loop child touch-eligibility fix.
- **S1 object destruction is only remembered for respawn-tracked layout entries, so non-tracked smashables reload fresh on an ObjPosLoad re-cross (MZ3 f13298 -> f14132):** `ObjectPlacementController.markRemembered` is now a no-op for non-respawn-tracked spawns. ROM `ObjPosLoad`'s `OPL_MakeItem` assigns `obRespawnNo` only when the layout id byte has its remember bit set; non-tracked entries keep `obRespawnNo == 0`, so `RememberState` deletes them without touching any respawn-table bit (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/sub RememberState.asm:16-21) and the next cursor crossing re-creates a fresh copy. The engine had marked every smashed object remembered, so MZ3's four below-screen MZ SmashBlocks (Obj0x51 @1110-1130,06F0-0710 — non-respawn-tracked) stayed permanently absent after the player smashed them, instead of reloading on the leftward `OPL_MovedLeft` ObjPosLoad pass the way ROM does. The persistent +4 OST occupancy deficit shifted the bounce-target Basaran (Obj0x55) ~4 slots low, off-phasing its vblank-gated dive `(v_vblank+(127-slot))&7` so the player missed the React_BadnikHit `+0x100` bounce (f13298 y_speed -0100 vs ROM 0). Gated on the ROM `respawnTracked` layout flag (S1 id-byte bit 7 / S2 yWord bit 15) — generic across zones/games, no zone/route/frame carve-out. MZ3 advances f13298 (449 errors) -> f14132 (447 errors, new x_speed frontier); all 15 S1 greens, the full S2 + S3K trace suites, the S3K must-keeps, and the rewind coverage guard stay green (10308 tests, only the 4 known S1 reds fail).
- **S1 SLZ seesaw tilt now tracks the riding player, not just the strict standing flag, so a rider who drifts to the edge still tilts (and drops off) the seesaw (SLZ3 f9866 -> f11325):** `Sonic1SeesawObjectInstance.update` now computes the seesaw tilt target (`See_ChkSide`/see_frame) whenever a player is riding it (SolidContacts riding state) and not airborne, instead of only while the narrow `playerStanding` flag is set. ROM `See_ChkSide` runs in routine 4, entered when `SlopeObject` lands a player (`addq.b #2,obRoutine`, `sub PlatformObject.asm:66`) and persisting until `ExitPlatform` unseats; see_frame then LATCHES while routine 2 (`See_Slope`) animates obFrame toward it (`5E SLZ Seesaw.asm:55-68`). Previously, when the rider's centre drifted 1px past the strict slope x-range, `validateStandingPlayer` cleared `playerStanding` and the seesaw stopped tilting: at SLZ3 f9862 a rider at seesaw @20A0's left edge left the seesaw stuck at frame 0 (raised left end), and three frames later that raised end caught the player who had correctly fallen off at f9863, re-landing him — while ROM, whose seesaw had latched to frame 2 (dropped left end), let him free-fall past it. S1-only (Obj0x5E is SLZ-only); comparison-only; no zone/route/frame carve-out. SLZ3 advances f9866 (147 errors) -> f11325 (65 errors); all 15 S1 trace greens (incl. SLZ1/SLZ2), S2 EHZ1, and the rewind coverage guard unchanged. docs/s1disasm/_incObj/5E SLZ Seesaw.asm:55-68; docs/s1disasm/_incObj/sub PlatformObject.asm:66,136.
- **S1 SLZ boss spikeball self-destruct fragments now spawn at the seesaw centre, so they can hurt a standing player (SLZ3 f7405 -> f9866):** When an SLZ boss spikeball (Obj0x7B) self-destructs on its seesaw it now spawns its explosion and four fragments at the seesaw-origin Y, matching ROM `BossSpikeball_MakeFrag`'s `move.w objoff_34(a0),obY(a0)` (objoff_34 = the linked seesaw's `obY`, set in `BossSpikeball_Main`). Previously `Sonic1SLZBossSpikeball.updateExploding` spawned them at the ball's offset resting position (`seesawY + BALL_Y_OFFSET`, ~8px too high), so a fragment that ROM places overlapping a standing player's hurt box sat just above it and never hurt — the engine kept the player grounded where ROM ran `Sonic_Hurt` (x_speed -0200, y_speed -0400, air 0->1). The reset is applied only on the self-destruct path (obSubtype == $20), which is reached exclusively from the RESTING routine where the ball is always linked to a seesaw; the boss-hit / flying-landing explosions clear obSubtype to 0 first and keep their current position. SLZ-boss-only (Obj0x7B is SLZ3-only); no zone/route/frame carve-out (gated on ROM object state). SLZ3 advances f7405 (261 errors) -> f9866 (147 errors); all S1 greens, S2 EHZ1, `TestS1SlzBossSpikeballGraphRewind`, and the rewind coverage guard unchanged. docs/s1disasm/_incObj/7A, 7B Boss - SLZ Main and Spike Balls.asm:535,833-864.
- **S1 SBZ object slot-cadence fidelity (SpinPlatform delete window + Walking-Bomb explosion/shrapnel slot allocation):** Three ROM-cited fixes to S1 object SST-slot lifecycle that drift the engine's OST occupancy away from the ROM (the upstream of the SBZ2 conveyor slot-cadence frontier). (1) The SBZ Spinning Platform / Trapdoor (Obj0x69) now unloads via the exact `out_of_range` macro (chunk-aligned, X-only, 640px window; `isInRange()`) instead of the approximate symmetric `isOnScreenX(160)`, which kept platforms ~160px left of the viewport alive after ROM `RememberState` had deleted them (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/69 SBZ Spinning Platforms and Trapdoors.asm:80,92,121; Macros.asm:273-289). (2) The Walking Bomb (Obj0x5F) timed self-explosion now changes the bomb into the explosion (Obj0x3F) IN PLACE, reusing the bomb's SST slot via the shared `detachSlotForTransfer`/`addReplacementAtTransferredSlot` badnik-kill path, matching ROM `_move.b #id_Explosion,obID(a0)` (Walking Bomb.asm:93-94), instead of spawning the explosion at the lowest free slot. (3) The Walking Bomb shrapnel now reuses the fuse's slot for piece 0 and allocates pieces 1-3 via `FindNextFreeObj` after the fuse slot, matching ROM `Bom_BurnFuseAndExplode` (Walking Bomb.asm:181-205), instead of lowest-free for all four; the fuse also unloads via `isInRange()` per its `RememberState` tail. These advance the SBZ2 first slot-occupancy divergence f1192 -> f1596 (bomb-cluster occupancy diff 20 -> 6 slots) but do NOT yet move the SBZ2 player-x frontier (still f2323, residual deep walking-bomb arm/explosion cadence — see TRACE_FRONTIER_LOG). Zero regression: all S1 greens (incl. SLZ1 walking bombs, SLZ2, SBZ1, SBZ3), S2 EHZ1, S3K must-keeps, and the rewind coverage guard stay green.
- **CI guard baseline refresh for S2 OOZ rewind work:** SlidingSpike peer links are now covered by the central object rewind policy instead of an object-local transient annotation, and the rewind tail inventory / release-critical source-size ratchets were synced to the current `develop` totals reported by CI.
- **S1 SLZ boss spikeball no longer springs the standing player on a no-tilt-change landing (SLZ3 f7198 -> f7405):** The freshly-dropped SLZ boss spikeball (Obj0x7B) landing on the side the seesaw is already tilted toward now correctly lands harmlessly and lets its spikes hurt the standing player, instead of catapulting them. `Sonic1SLZBossSpikeball.transitionToSeesawResting` was missing the first of ROM `loc_18FA2`'s two launch guards — `cmp.b obFrame(a1),d1 / beq.s loc_19008`, which skips the launch when the landing tilt angle equals the seesaw's current visual frame (so a ball that does not flip the seesaw cannot launch the rider). It launched whenever a player was standing, flinging Sonic up (`y_speed -07E0`) on the landing frame. A BizHawk PC-probe established the ROM ground truth that the player here is HURT, not sprung: at trace f7199 the player's `obVelY` is set by `move.w #-$400,obVelY(a0)` with `a0=player` (`Sonic_Hurt` knockback; `x_vel -$200`, anim `$1A`, a lost-rings Obj0x37 spawns), not by the ball spring. The fix gates the launch on `landingAngle != seesaw.getMappingFrame()` (obFrame, read before the tilt-target update) AND-ed with the existing standing-player check. SLZ-boss-only (Obj0x7B is SLZ3-only); the regular SLZ seesaw ball (Obj0x5E) is untouched and SLZ1/SLZ2 stay green; no zone/route/frame carve-out (gated on ROM object/tilt state). SLZ3 advances f7198 (217 errors) -> f7405 (261 errors); all S1 greens, S2 EHZ1, and the rewind coverage guard unchanged. The new f7405 frontier is a separate, deeper second hurt by another resting spikeball/fragment (see TRACE_FRONTIER_LOG). docs/s1disasm/_incObj/7A, 7B Boss - SLZ Main and Spike Balls.asm:776-806.
- **S1 SLZ boss spikeball drop cadence + launch fall-through (SLZ3 f6507 -> f7198):** The SLZ boss (Obj0x7A) now reproduces ROM `BSLZ_MakeBall`'s `.checkForBall` duplicate-abort, and the boss spikeball (Obj0x7B) applies its first flight step on the launch frame. Previously the boss dropped a spikeball on *every* scan alignment (engine ~80 drops vs ROM ~5) because the duplicate check was absent, so balls were never positioned to spring the player on the ROM frame. `Sonic1SLZBossInstance.updateBallSpawn` now scans active boss spikeballs for one already pointing at the target seesaw (`getTargetSeesaw()==target`, non-fragment) and aborts the drop (back to SCANNING with BossMove+sine) when found — using the released-ROM `FixBugs=0` half-pool scan range (object slots 1..63 only, so a duplicate ball that spilled into a slot `>= 64` is invisible to the buggy scan, exactly reproducing ROM's two-balls-on-one-seesaw cadence; the engine `SlotAllocator` is FindFreeObj-faithful with S1 dynamic slots 32-127). Separately, `Sonic1SLZBossSpikeball.launchFromSeesaw` now falls through to `updateFlying()` on the launch frame, mirroring ROM `BossSpikeball_Bounce`'s `addq.b #2,obRoutine(a0) / bra.w BossSpikeball_HitBoss` (the launch frame runs the flying routine and applies its first ObjectFall the same frame) — the same fall-through already modelled on the seesaw's own spikeball — which removed a 1-frame lag in the ball's flight and the landing that springs the standing player. SLZ-boss-only (Obj0x7A/0x7B are SLZ3-only); no zone/route/frame carve-out (gated on ROM object state + the documented `FixBugs` revision behavior). SLZ3 advances f6507 (249 errors) -> f7198 (217 errors); all S1 greens, S2 EHZ1, and the rewind coverage guard unchanged. The new f7198 frontier is a separate deeper freshly-dropped-ball landing/halving sub-frame timing on seesaw 38 (see TRACE_FRONTIER_LOG). docs/s1disasm/_incObj/7A, 7B Boss - SLZ Main and Spike Balls.asm:275-285,307-309 (.checkForBall / FixBugs half-pool / .abortDrop), 610-614 (BossSpikeball_Bounce fall-through).
- **S2 OOZ parity pass resolves reviewed object gaps:** Added Obj55 Oil Ocean boss dispatch, arena event spawn path, PLC/art registrations, and focused boss/event tests; tightened OOZ launcher/launcher-ball multi-player capture, ball snapping, fragment frames, and active-capture cleanup; expanded Obj15 bit-7 SwingingPlatform split/falling-child state; corrected Aquis projectile spawn side, ROM bullet animation/priority, shooting-window consumption, and wing/projectile rewind state; aligned Octus floor-anchor snapping with its ROM floor radius; kept pressure springs/checkpoints, SlidingSpike audio/priority, and OilSurface multi-player entry state closer to disassembly behavior. The pass also routes newly touched boss destruction and playable native y-position writes through shared object/player helpers so architecture guards stay flat.
- **Swinging-platform (Obj0x15) chain links unload with the parent pivot, not on their own swung-out position — S1 MZ3 f9917 -> f13298:** `Sonic1SwingingPlatformObjectInstance.SwingChainLinkChild` now overrides `getOutOfRangeReferenceX()` to return the parent's pivot X (`swing_origX`) instead of inheriting the default (the link's current swinging position). In ROM the chain links run routine `$A` (`Swing_Display` = just `bra.w DisplaySprite`) and have **no** `out_of_range` check of their own; the whole assembly is deleted en masse by the parent's `Swing_ChkDel: out_of_range.w Swing_DelAll,swing_origX(a0)`, keyed on the parent's original X (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/15 Swinging Platforms.asm:247-248,278-279). The engine modelled the links as real OST-slot children (correct, for FindFreeObj-occupancy parity) but let each one self-despawn when its swung position left the camera window, so a link that swung off-screen while the pivot was still on-screen unloaded early and freed its SST slot ahead of ROM. On S1 MZ3 this dropped a 12-segment chain to 10 one frame after spawn (trace f6313 12 -> f6314 10), shifting the co-located lava-ball-maker (Obj0x13) down a slot and permuting every downstream FindFreeObj allocation, which eventually placed a Batbrain (Obj0x55) at slot 81 instead of 82 — changing its vblank-gated `(v_vblank_byte+(127-slot))&7` drop frame and bouncing the player one frame early (`y_speed` -04D8 vs -05D8 at f9917). Keying the link's unload on the pivot makes every piece unload on the same frame as the parent, matching `Swing_DelAll`. The pivot field is un-finaled so the generic rewind field capturer reapplies it after a recreate. S1 MZ3 advances f9917 (664 errors) -> f13298 (449 errors); all S1 greens (incl. GHZ/SLZ1/SLZ2/SBZ1/SBZ3/MZ1, which also use Obj0x15), S2 EHZ1, and the rewind coverage guard unchanged. docs/s1disasm/_incObj/15 Swinging Platforms.asm (Swing_Main .makechain, Swing_Display, Swing_ChkDel, Swing_DelAll).
- **S1 tall hurt objects stay touchable via the ROM custom-height render flag (MZ lava geyser column):** `AbstractObjectInstance.isOnScreenForTouch()` now mirrors the S1 `BuildSprites` custom-height path: an object that sets `obRender` bit 4 (`bset #4,obRender`) has its touch-response render-flag Y gate computed from its own `obHeight` half-extent (`cameraBounds.containsRenderSpriteBounds`) instead of the fixed 32px `.assumeHeight` band. The MZ lava geyser column (Obj0x4D body) is a 256px-tall hurt object (`col_64x224|col_hurt`, `obHeight=#256/2=$80`) whose anchor `y` sits above the camera top while the column still overlaps the screen; the old fixed-32px gate wrongly treated it as off-screen (`offscreenTouch`) and skipped `ReactToItem`, so a player standing under the falling column was never hurt. A new `AbstractObjectInstance.usesCustomRenderHeight()` predicate (default `false`) models the ROM render-flag bit, overridden only by the lava geyser BODY piece (which also reports `getOnScreenHalfHeight()=$80`); all other objects are unchanged. ROM render-flag model, not a zone/object carve-out. Necessary for the MZ geyser hurt to fire at all; zero trace regression (13 S1 greens, S2 EHZ1, rewind coverage guard all unchanged; MZ1/MZ3 frontiers unchanged). MZ2's remaining f2823 divergence is a separate lavafall eruption-cadence phase offset (see TRACE_FRONTIER_LOG). docs/s1disasm/_inc/BuildSprites.asm:61-73 (custom-height Y test); docs/s1disasm/_incObj/Sonic ReactToItem.asm:50-51 (obRender bit-7 gate); docs/s1disasm/_incObj/"4C, 4D MZ Lava Geyser and Maker.asm":213-214 (obHeight=$80, bset #4 obRender).
- **Camera horizontal level boundary is applied directionally (ROM `MoveScreenHoriz`), not as a symmetric clamp — S1 LZ1 GREEN:** `Camera.computeNextHorizontalCameraX` now clamps the camera against the left boundary (`minX` / ROM `v_limitleft2`) ONLY on the leftward-scroll branch and against the right boundary (`maxX` / ROM `v_limitright2`) ONLY on the rightward-scroll branch, with no boundary clamp at all in the sweet-spot (no-scroll) path, exactly matching ROM `MoveScreenHoriz` (`SH_MoveCameraLeft` consults `v_limitleft2`, `SH_MoveCameraRight` consults `v_limitright2`). The previous code applied a symmetric `clampAxisWithWrap(x, minX, maxX)` every frame (and a redundant second symmetric clamp in `updatePosition`). At the end of an act the signpost (Obj0x0D `Sign_Touch`) executes `move.w (v_limitright2).w,(v_limitleft2).w` to lock the screen, but because Sonic keeps running right the camera only ever consults `v_limitright2`, so the raised left boundary is invisible and the camera continues tracking the player up to the right limit. The engine's symmetric clamp instead yanked the camera UP to the new `minX` a few frames early. Fixes S1 LZ1 complete-run trace at f12463 (`camera_x` expected 0x19B3, was 0x19BF) — the engine reached the right scroll limit 0x19BF two frames before ROM. The redundant per-frame symmetric horizontal re-clamp in `updatePosition` was removed (the directional clamp inside `computeNextHorizontalCameraX` is authoritative); the SCZ-style wrapped-domain (`maxX < minX`) handling is preserved in `clampRightBoundary`. S1 LZ1 RED -> GREEN; all S1 greens, S2 EHZ1, S3K critical/AIZ, and the 26 `TestCamera` unit tests unchanged (S1/S2/S3K reds byte-identical to baseline). docs/s1disasm/_inc/ScrollHoriz & ScrollVertical.asm (MoveScreenHoriz, SH_MoveCameraLeft, SH_MoveCameraRight); docs/s1disasm/_incObj/0D Signpost.asm (Sign_Touch).
- **S2 OOZ placed-object coverage reaches 100%:** Added Oil Ocean `Obj43` SlidingSpike and `Obj45` OOZ pressure spring with ROM-backed art/mappings, registry/profile coverage, focused subtype/solid/spring tests, and PLC dispatch registrations. The S2 object discovery report now shows 122/122 placed objects implemented; the remaining OOZ parity item is the dynamic `Obj55` boss. Cleaned stale Sonic 2 PLC TODO comments whose art is loaded through provider/shared paths, and clarified ChopChop's live small-bubble parity gap.
- **S1 LZ Burrobot walks off ledges (ObjFloorDist returns a fall distance, not "no surface"):** The S1 LZ Burrobot (Obj0x2D) `Burro_Action_Move` floor handling now mirrors ROM `ObjFloorDist`/`FindFloor`, which always returns a distance: when neither the sensor tile nor the tile below is solid (the Burrobot has walked off a ledge), `FindFloor2.isblank2` returns `$F - (sensorY & $F)` and `FindFloor.isblank` adds `$10`, giving `$1F - (sensorY & $F)` — a small positive fall distance — and `alignToFloor` adds it unconditionally (`add.w d1,obY`). The engine's shared `ObjectTerrainUtils.checkFloorDist` reports the both-blank case as no-collision, and the Burrobot's `alignToFloor` guarded the descent with `if (foundSurface())`, so off a ledge the Burrobot walked on air instead of falling, never reached its random `Burro_Action_Move_NextAction` jump, and turned around on the spot. In LZ1 that left a Burrobot grounded at the player's jump-off point, so Sonic's launch killed it 9 frames early (a `React_BadnikHit.slowFromBelow` `+$100` bounce at f12271 instead of the ROM bounce at f12280). `Sonic1BurrobotBadnikInstance.updateMove` now uses a private `objFloorDist()` that substitutes the ROM blank-tile return when `checkFloorDist` reports no surface, and adds it unconditionally for both the floor-align and ledge-check probes. Object-local S1 fix (Obj0x2D is LZ-only); no shared-primitive change, no zone/route/frame carve-out. Fixes S1 LZ1 trace divergence at f12271 (frontier f12271 -> f12463, collapsing the f12271->f12517 cascade to a single 2-frame end-of-act `camera_x` transient); LZ2/LZ3 stay green. docs/s1disasm/_incObj/2D Badnik - Burrobot.asm:66-91; docs/s1disasm/_incObj/sub ObjFloorDist.asm; docs/s1disasm/_incObj/sub FindNearestTile & FindFloor & FindWall.asm (FindFloor.isblank, FindFloor2.isblank2); docs/s1disasm/_incObj/Sonic ReactToItem.asm:296-309.
- **S1 Egg Prison does not lock the camera at the switch trigger (LZ3 GREEN):** The S1 Egg Prison capsule (Obj0x3E) no longer freezes the camera (`camera.setMinX(getX())` / `camera.setMaxX(getX())`) when the player lands on the release switch. ROM `Pri_Switch` on the switch-stood frame only stops the timer, clears `f_lockscreen`, locks controls, and forces right input (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/3E Prison Capsule.asm:97-99`); it never writes `v_limitleft2`/`v_limitright2`, so the camera keeps scrolling to `v_limitright2`. For every act-3 boss zone that value is the LevelSizeArray boundary expanded by the boss escape's `addq.w #2,(v_limitright2)` up to `boss_*_end` (LZ: `$202F` -> `boss_lz_end=$2031`). The engine's lock pinned `maxX`/camera at the value it held when the player landed on the switch; in LZ3 that is ~10px short of `v_limitright2` (the player reaches the switch before the camera finishes scrolling), so `camera_x` froze 1px under ROM and drifted as ROM scrolled `0x2027 -> 0x2031` (player runs off-screen right to `0x2199` via `Sonic_LevelBound`, `_incObj/01 Sonic.asm:1045-1049`). The old "camera stays put because v_limitleft2 = v_limitright2" comment was the Signpost end-of-act path (`0D Signpost.asm:54,163`), which act-3 boss zones never run (`SignpostArtLoad` skips act 3, `sonic.asm:3164-3165`). Object-local to Obj0x3E (shared by GHZ3/MZ3/SYZ3/SLZ3/LZ3); GHZ3 and SYZ3 already had the camera at the boundary at trigger time so the removed lock was a no-op for them. Fixes S1 LZ3 trace divergence at f18196 (LZ3 complete-run now GREEN — 14th S1 green); no zone/route/frame carve-out.
- **Rolling turnaround inertia clamp on sign change:** When the player rolls into the opposite direction and the inertia crosses through exactly zero, the rightward turnaround now clamps inertia to `+$80` (keeping the player rolling) instead of letting it settle at 0 and unrolling. ROM `Sonic_RollRight.changedirection` does `add.w d4,d0 / bcc / move.w #$80,d0`: the `add` sets the carry when the signed result is `>= 0` (including exactly 0), so the clamp fires on an exact-zero crossing. The mirror `Sonic_RollLeft.changeddirection` uses `sub.w d4,d0 / bcc / move.w #-$80,d0`, whose subtraction borrows only when the result is strictly negative, so a leftward exact-zero crossing correctly stays at 0 and unrolls. The engine's `PlayableSpriteMovement.doRollSpeed` right-turnaround used `if (gSpeed > 0)`, missing the exact-zero case; it now uses `if (gSpeed >= 0)` while the left turnaround keeps `< 0`. Shared S1/S2/S3K physics (all three games use the identical add-carry/sub-borrow asymmetry); no zone/route/frame carve-out. Fixes S1 LZ1 trace divergence at f12097 (frontier f12097 -> f12271): the ROM player rolling left and pressing right kept rolling at `+$7A` while the engine unrolled and stopped. docs/s1disasm/_incObj/01 Sonic.asm:871-878,895-899; docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:37119-37146; docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm sub_11608/sub_1162C.
- **S1 LZ conveyor re-spawns its platform cluster on re-entry:** The S1 LZ Conveyor (Obj0x63) now clears its maker's `v_obj63` "already spawned" latch when the platform cluster leaves the screen, so the spawner re-creates the moving platforms each time the player returns — instead of spawning them only once. The maker latches `bset #0,(v_obj63,slot)` on its first spawn and self-deletes if the bit is already set; ROM releases that latch in the children's `out_of_range` tail (`loc_12378`: only the child whose `objoff_2F` is negative — "platform #0", the maker's reincarnated slot — runs `bclr #0,(v_obj63,slot)`), so the cluster re-spawns on re-entry (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/63 LZ Conveyor.asm:22-28,95-112). The engine implemented the spawn-side latch and the platform-#0 slot reuse but never cleared the latch, so after the first visit every group's moving platforms were gone permanently (only the decorative wheels, subtype 0x7F, remained) and a player falling down the conveyor loop dropped straight through where ROM lands him on a re-spawned platform. `Sonic1LZConveyorObjectInstance` now tags platform #0 with the maker's dedup slot (`makerDedupSlot`) and adds an `onUnload()` that calls `Sonic1ConveyorState.clearSpawned(makerDedupSlot)` on the out_of_range path (gated `mode==PLATFORM && initialized && !isDestroyed()`), mirroring the existing `Sonic1SpinConveyorObjectInstance` precedent. Only platform #0 clears the latch (exactly ROM's `objoff_2F`-negative gating), and it clears the maker's v_obj63 index rather than the child path group. S1-only (Obj0x63 is LZ-only); no zone/route/frame carve-out. Fixes S1 LZ1 trace divergence at f9716 (frontier f9716 -> f12097) and S1 LZ3 at f11802 (frontier f11802 -> f18196).
- **S1/S2 water level advances before the player's underwater check:** The dynamic water level (move toward target) now runs BEFORE player physics for S1 and S2, matching ROM `LZWaterFeatures`/`WaterEffects` executing before `ExecuteObjects`/`RunObjects` (S3K is unchanged — its `Process_Sprites` runs before `Handle_Onscreen_Water_Height`, so the player reads the previous-frame level there). Previously the engine moved the water level in the post-physics level update (`LevelManager.update()`, after the player's `Sonic_Water` check), so while the water was rising the player read a 1px-stale water base and crossed the surface one frame late. In S1 LZ that delayed the ROM water-EXIT velocity doubling (`asl.w obVelY`, `docs/s1disasm/_incObj/01 Sonic.asm:295`): the player's upward `y_speed` came out un-doubled (-0x270 instead of -0x4E0) on the exit frame and doubled one frame later. New `PhysicsFeatureSet.advanceWaterLevelBeforePlayerPhysics` (true S1/S2, false S3K) gates a pre-physics `LevelManager.advanceDynamicWaterLevel()` step in `LevelFrameStep`; `LevelManager.update()` skips the move when the flag is set. Per-game ROM-ordering model (no zone/route/frame carve-out). Fixes S1 LZ1 trace divergence at f8285 (frontier f8285 -> f9716); S1 LZ3 also advanced. docs/s1disasm/sonic.asm:2986-2987; docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:5094-5095; docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm Process_Sprites/Handle_Onscreen_Water_Height.
- **S1 LZ Harpoon AnimateSprite cadence:** The S1 LZ Harpoon (Obj0x16) now reproduces ROM `AnimateSprite` timing, so each extend/retract animation frame displays for the ROM's 4 game-frames and the 2-frame animate phase runs 9 frames instead of 8. The engine pre-loaded `currentFrame=sequence[0]` with `animFrameTimer=3`, so it showed the first frame for only 3 frames, transitioned to the second frame one frame early, and lost a frame every cycle — accumulating phase drift that left the harpoon one animation step more extended than ROM. With the harpoon stuck on a longer (`col_8x48`) frame instead of ROM's retracted (`col_8x16`) frame, its taller hurt box reached the rolling player and triggered a spurious HURT bounce the ROM never delivers. `Sonic1HarpoonObjectInstance.updateAnimation` now mirrors ROM `Anim_Run` (decrement, wait while `>=0`, else reload the duration byte then load `sequence[index]` and post-increment, or fire `afRoutine`); the constructor seeds the post-init state of ROM's Harp_Main→Harp_Move fall-through (`animFrameIndex=1`); and the `updateWait` extend/retract toggle zeroes the duration counter/index (the ROM anim-change reset) leaving the previous frame until the next update advances. Fixes S1 LZ1 trace divergence at f7325 (frontier f7325 -> f8285). docs/s1disasm/_incObj/sub AnimateSprite.asm; docs/s1disasm/_incObj/16 LZ Harpoon.asm; docs/s1disasm/_anim/Harpoon.asm.
- **S1 LZ conveyor maker reuses its own SST slot for platform #0:** The S1 LZ Conveyor maker (Obj0x63, subtype bit 7) now reuses its own object slot for the first belt platform instead of spawning all platforms as fresh `FindFreeObj` children and deleting itself. ROM `LCon_Main` (loc_12460) does `movea.l a0,a1 / bra.s LCon_MakePtfms`, turning the maker into platform #0 in its own slot (obRoutine stays 0, so #0's first `PlatformObject`/`SpeedToPos` runs the following frame); only platforms #1..N use `FindFreeObj` (`LCon_Loop`, non-FixBugs REV01 path) (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/63 LZ Conveyor.asm:95-145). By spawning platform #0 as a fresh lowest-free child, the engine shifted every later platform up one SST slot, so a descending-leg platform that ROM places BELOW the maker's slot (already processed that frame -> first move next frame) instead landed ABOVE it (executed same frame). That left every belt platform one executed frame / 1px ahead of ROM, and a ridden platform dropped the player 1px low. `Sonic1LZConveyorObjectInstance.updateSpawner()` now detaches its own slot (`ObjectLifetimeOps.detachSlotForTransfer`) and forces platform #0 into it (same maker pattern as `Sonic1LavaGeyserMakerObjectInstance`); platforms #1..N keep `FindFreeObj`. Matches the ROM slot set {44,72,92,96,97,98,99,100} and per-platform first-move cadence. Fixes S1 LZ1 trace divergence at f5745 (frontier f5745 -> f7325).
- **S1 collapsing-floor NoReset fragment keeps rider seated:** The S1 collapsing floor (Obj0x53, MZ/SLZ/SBZ) now holds its rider in place on the routine-4 `Fragmentate_8x2Floor_NoReset` frame instead of unseating him one frame early. ROM `CFlo_OnPlatform` branches to `Fragmentate_8x2Floor_NoReset` when the collapse timer hits zero and SKIPS the fall-through to `CFlo_WalkOff` (ExitPlatform + MvSonicOnPtfm2) that every other routine-4 frame runs, so the rider is neither re-seated nor unseated on the fragment frame — he keeps `Status_OnObj` and only walks off the next frame via routine-6 `CFlo_FragmentPiece .delayCollapse` (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/1A, 53 Collapsing Ledges and Floors.asm:203-205, 210-216, 228-231). Because the engine evaluates the continued-riding solid pass AFTER each object's `update()`, the still-routine-4 floor saw the rider already past its X-band and unseated him a frame early (player `air` 0->1). `Sonic1CollapsingFloorObjectInstance` now reports the pending-NoReset-fragment frame (`routine==4 && collapseFlag && collapseDelay<=0 && !fragmented`) through `suppressSlopeSampleThisFrame`/`defersAirborneRiderUnseatThisFrame`, so the shared `ObjectSolidContactController` keeps the grounded rider seated that one frame. Keyed purely on ROM state (routine + `objoff_38` timer + collapse flag), it fires for SLZ's walk-off rider and MZ's collapse-release rider identically and is a no-op for any rider already off the band. Reconciled against MZ3's v3.12 `objoff_38` collapse-timer ground truth: SLZ1 trace now GREEN (full run); MZ3 unchanged at f9917 (NOT regressed to f2173). The `collapseEnteredThisFrame` routine-4 deferral is retained — it aligns the fragment timing with ROM for both encounters.
- **S1 SLZ staircase reserved-child-slot leak:** The S1 SLZ staircase (Obj0x5B) now keys its 3-slot child reservation by its stable placement spawn instead of `getSpawn()`. Because the staircase calls `updateDynamicSpawn` every frame, `getSpawn()` returned a per-frame `dynamicSpawn` whose identity never matched the construction-time placement spawn that `ObjectManager.freeAllReservedChildSlots` uses on out-of-range unload, so each unloading staircase leaked its 3 reserved dynamic SST slots. Across the SLZ1 act five reloading staircases exhausted the 96-slot dynamic pool, starving ObjPosLoad's `FindFreeObj` so the SLZ fireball maker (Obj0x13) reloaded one 0x80 chunk late and its rightward fireball (Obj0x14) reached the player ~55 frames behind ROM — the player rode the staircase through a hit the ROM delivers. Keying by the placement `spawn` field (as ChainedStomper, RingInstance, AizGiantRideVine and MGZSwingingPlatform already do) lets the reservations free on unload. Fixes SLZ1 trace divergence at f3250 (frontier f3250 -> f3520). docs/s1disasm/_inc/ObjPosLoad.asm OPL_MovedLeft; docs/s1disasm/_incObj/13, 14 MZ, SLZ Fire Balls and Maker.asm.
- **S1 Caterkiller multi-segment body despawn sync:** The S1 Caterkiller (Obj0x78) body segments now free their SST slots on the same frame as the head, instead of one frame early, when the head despawns off-screen. ROM `Cat_Despawn` sets the head's `obRoutine = $A` and `rts` (frame N); the body segments, executing after the head, detect the head's routine $A the same frame, set their own routine $A and (REV01 `FixBugs = 0`) fall through to `DisplaySprite`, then `Cat_Delete` → `DeleteObject` deletes the head and all segments together on frame N+1 (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/78 Badnik - Caterkiller.asm:139-152,368-391`). The engine's head removed at the ROM frame, but the off-screen body segments were culled one frame early by the generic `out_of_range` pass: `Sonic1CaterkillerBodyInstance.isPersistent()` returned false the frame `head.isDeleting()` flipped (before `head.isDestroyed()`), and that frame is before each segment's own `update()` can latch its deferred delete. Gating persistence on `!head.isDestroyed()` (the head's slot still being live) lets each segment survive that frame, latch its delete, and free in sync with the head. Verified: the Caterkiller body chain (slots 66/67/106) now frees at f1335 (matching ROM) instead of f1334, and the SBZ2 conveyor (Obj0x68) that the early free had pushed to engine slot 79 now lands on ROM slot 66. (SBZ2 trace frontier f2323 still holds — a further slot-62 conveyor↔lost-ring placement-pass interleave remains downstream — see TRACE_FRONTIER_LOG.) Resolves the f1334 Caterkiller-body slot divergence exposed by the SBZ small door fix below.
- **S1 SBZ small door out_of_range despawn:** The S1 SBZ small door (Obj0x2A `AutoDoor`) now despawns through the ROM `out_of_range` window instead of an over-permissive symmetric `isOnScreenX(160)` margin. ROM `ADoor_OpenShut` ends with `bra.w RememberState`, which deletes the door via the plain `out_of_range` macro (chunk-aligned, unloads at ~`camX-128`); the old 160px margin held the door alive ~32px too long off the left edge, freeing its SST slot one ObjPosLoad batch late. That delayed free inverted the slot allocation of objects spawned afterward (matching the sibling StomperDoor Obj0x69, which already uses `isInRangeAt`). Advances the SBZ2 first slot-occupancy divergence from f1080 to f1334. docs/s1disasm/_incObj/2A SBZ Small Door.asm:55; docs/s1disasm/_incObj/sub RememberState.asm:8-9. (SBZ2 trace frontier f2323 remains gated downstream by the Caterkiller Obj0x78 multi-segment body despawn ordering — see TRACE_FRONTIER_LOG.)
- **S1 LZ air-bubble maker pool-full RNG retry:** The S1 LZ air-bubble maker (Obj0x64 `Bub_BblMaker`) now replicates ROM's `FindFreeObj` failure path: after consuming its spawn-delay `RandomNumber & $1F`, it tests for a free dynamic SST slot and, when the pool is full, bails before the bubble-X-offset (`& $F`) and large-bubble 25%-override (`& 3`) `RandomNumber` draws and before spawning the child — exactly ROM `bne.s .fail` — while the caller's `objoff_34` decrement (and optional long-delay `& $7F` draw) still runs. Previously the engine always consumed the xOffset/override `RandomNumber` even when its `spawnFreeChild` silently dropped the bubble, pushing the shared RNG ahead of the ROM. This is the sibling of the LZ drowning-countdown pool-full fix and completes ROM RNG-cadence parity for the LZ air-bubble system. docs/s1disasm/_incObj/64 LZ Air Bubbles.asm:166-205. (LZ3 trace frontier f8499 remains gated by a separate co-located-maker slot-order RNG interleave — see TRACE_FRONTIER_LOG.)
- **CI ROM-missing log hygiene:** configured missing ROM files now fail before `Rom.open()` logs SEVERE stack traces, so headless scroll and palette loaders can degrade through their existing `IOException` handling without flooding GitHub CI logs.
- **Rewind generic recreate hardening:** parent-linked probe constructors now skip safely when no live parent candidate exists, and dynamic recreate contexts reject null object managers before restore-time object services are queried.
- **S1 LZ drowning-countdown pool-full RNG retry:** The S1 LZ air/drowning countdown (Obj0x0A `Drown_Countdown`) now replicates ROM's `FindFreeObj` failure path: when the 96-slot dynamic object pool is full it still consumes the spawn-interval `RandomNumber` but does NOT spawn a bubble, advance `objoff_34`, or clear the `objoff_36` production flag — so it keeps retrying (one `RandomNumber` per interval) until a slot frees, exactly like the ROM. Previously the engine always "spawned" (silently dropped when full) and stopped retrying several intervals early, leaving the shared RNG behind the ROM and mispositioning the next RNG-derived spawn. Fixes the S1 LZ2 air-bubble (Obj0x64) X drift (trace frontier f7800 -> f8491). docs/s1disasm/_incObj/0A LZ Drowning Countdown.asm:280-340. Adds non-mutating `ObjectManager.hasFreeDynamicSlot()` / `SlotAllocator.hasFreeSlot()` ROM `FindFreeObj` probes.
- **S1 SLZ seesaw full-width top landing:** The SLZ seesaw (Obj0x5E) now uses its full `obActWid` (0x30) as the top-landing width instead of the generic `obActWid - $B` narrowing, matching ROM `See_Slope`/`See_Slope2` which pass `#96/2` directly into `SlopeObject`/`SlopeObject_AssumeStoodOn` with no narrowing (then `bra Plat_NoXCheck_AltY`, which skips any further X check). A player falling onto the raised end of the seesaw near its edge now re-lands like ROM instead of falling through. Fixes SLZ3 trace divergence at f6364 (frontier f6364 -> f6507). Matches the sibling SlopeObject users CollapsingLedge (Obj0x53) and CollapsingFloor (Obj0x1A).
- **S1 monitor break child-spawn timing:** The S1 monitor (Obj0x26) now defers its power-up (Obj0x2E) and explosion (Obj0x27) `FindFreeObj` spawns from the player touch pass to its own object execution, matching ROM `Mon_BreakOpen` (which runs in the monitor's SST slot, not `ReactToItem`). This lets the explosion — which lands in a lower SST slot than the monitor — defer its first `ExecuteObjects` frame, so it no longer expires one frame early and frees its slot a frame ahead of ROM. Fixes the S1 LZ2 -1 SST-slot offset cascade (trace frontier f6418 -> f7800). docs/s1disasm/_incObj/26, 2E Monitors and Power-Ups.asm:181-198; docs/s1disasm/_incObj/27, 3F Explosions.asm:30-53.
- **S1 SLZ boss seesaw spring-launch:** The SLZ boss spikeball (Obj0x7B) now flings a standing player off the seesaw with the ROM `loc_18FA2` velocity and roll state. The boss (Obj0x7A) creates the ball on its first `BSLZ_MakeBall` frame (not the scanning match frame) so it spawns at the post-`BossMove` position and falls the correct number of gravity steps; the ball no longer clears its vertical speed before the launch reads it; and the launch now halves the velocity when the seesaw is flat (`asr.w obVelY`) and routes the player through the ROM `Sonic_ChkRoll` ball-entry (clearing the jump flag and shifting y_pos down by the standing/rolling radius difference). Fixes SLZ3 trace divergence at f6113 (frontier f6113 -> f6364).
- **S1 SYZ1 wall-detach slope-resist fix:** The shared player-physics missed-detach slope-resist replay no longer re-applies walking slope resistance on a wall-detach frame when the player was stationary at frame start, matching ROM `Sonic_SlopeResistWalk`'s `tst.w inertia / beq` early return (S1 01 Sonic.asm:1308-1309, S2/S3K equivalents). - **S1 SLZ boss spikeball hurt box:** The SLZ boss spikeball (Obj0x7B) now reports its ROM-centre position from `getX()`/`getY()` instead of the sprite top-left, so its `col_16x16` hurt box is placed correctly and a rolling player rising into the falling ball is hurt on the ROM frame (SLZ3 trace f5917 -> f6113).

### v0.6.prerelease (Current development snapshot)

The active 0.6 prerelease line is focused on S3K vertical-slice parity, trace-driven ROM accuracy, release hardening, and gameplay-scoped rewind reliability. Detailed per-frontier notes were moved out of this top-level changelog so it stays readable; see [docs/status/trace-frontier-log.md](docs/status/trace-frontier-log.md) for frame-by-frame trace evidence and [docs/changelog/v0.6-prerelease-detailed.md](docs/changelog/v0.6-prerelease-detailed.md) for the previous verbose merge ledger.

- **S3K LBZ2 post-boss Death Egg finale parity:** the LBZ2 first Robotnik post-results handoff now leaves the score tally under boss control, restores the level music, queues the boss-explosion and small Death Egg art, drives Sonic/Tails through the ROM external-player mapping-frame sequence, plays explosion SFX from the launch-pad emitters, deletes Death Egg explosion debris through `Sprite_CheckDeleteXY` bounds, starts the Death Egg final fall transition, and keeps the foreground launch pad V-scroll coupled to the launch camera before the detach counter begins so Sonic no longer appears to sink through the platform.

- **S3K LBZ2 launch screen shake follows ROM camera copies:** the Act 2 launch/deformation path now applies `Screen_shake_offset` to the foreground Plane A camera copy and to the background V-scroll value used for deformation band lookup, while avoiding a second BG shake add in the Death Egg-specific deform path.

- **S3K LBZ2 object coverage:** Pipe Plug, Spin Launcher, Lowering Grapple, and Gate Laser now route through the S3KL/LBZ object table with ROM-backed mappings/art, focused behavior tests, and LBZ-only profile coverage. The Pipe Plug, Spin Launcher, and Lowering Grapple no longer self-delete from an X+Y viewport check; they now rely on the standard ROM-style X-only object unload path so placements stay visible in-game and in the debug overlay.

- **S3K LBZ2 first Robotnik fight faces inward on both sides:** the LBZ final boss Robotnik head child now inherits the parent ship's horizontal render flag after each random side reposition, matching `Obj_RobotnikHead3`/`Refresh_ChildPositionAdjusted` so Robotnik faces right from the left side of the arena and left from the right side.

- **S1 FZ is GREEN (f4128 -> end), S1's 10th green trace — three FZ-boss escape fixes resolve the escape-sprite roll-bounce tail:** (1) The FZ boss (`Sonic1FZBossInstance`, Obj0x85) escape-sequence position clamps now preserve the 16.16 subpixel via new `clampYPreservingSubpixel`/`clampXPreservingSubpixel` helpers (keep `*Fixed & 0xFFFF`, replace only the high word), matching the ROM `move.w #imm,obY(a0)` WORD stores at the defeat-onset, defeat-fall landing (`boss_fz_y+$8C`), running-escape x-cap (`boss_fz_x+$250`), and final-ascent landing (`boss_fz_y+$82`). Zeroing the fraction with `y << 16` lost up to ~1px per clamp across the slow escape ascent (`BossFinal_Eggman_Escape` velY=-$18 = 0.094px/frame), leaving the boss 1px high (y=0x053F vs ROM 0x0540) so the rolling player's `React_BossHit` touch (carry-edge overlap) missed at f4128 and the neg/neg/asr/asr rebound (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/Sonic ReactToItem.asm:260-263`) fired one frame late. (2) `updateFinalFlight`'s post-hit `$1E` timer expiry now re-arms `col_48x48|col_boss` only when the boss is NOT defeated (`tst.b obStatus / bpl loc_1A210`); the single escape hit takes `obBossHits` 1->0 and sets the defeated bit, so the boss falls (velY=$60) and stays `col_none` — the prior on-screen check produced an extra roll-bounce ROM never makes (was f4182). (3) The control-lock at `boss_fz_end+$90` now clears inertia only (`clr.w (v_player+obInertia)`), never `obVelX`, so the airborne rolling player keeps `x_speed`=0x0255 (was the f4200 `x_speed`=0 divergence). ROM cites `docs/s1disasm/_incObj/85,84,86 Boss - FZ Main, Cylinders, and Plasma Balls.asm:234-497`. ROM `Swing_Main` allocates one SST slot per chain link via FindFreeObj and sets each link to routine $A (`Swing_Display`) — the links just display while the anchor positions them in `Swing_Move2` (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/15 Swinging Platforms.asm:67-105,215-241`); the links carry no collision (only the anchor/ball is solid/hurt). The engine previously modelled the whole chain as one object with internal link arrays, so each chain occupied 1 OST slot vs ROM's `chainCount+1`; in SBZ2 the ~8-slot deficit shifted the Walking Bombs (Obj 0x5F) down from ROM slots 0x69-0x6C to 0x64-0x67 (`obj_s69_slot exp 0x69 act 0x64`). The engine folds the staircase into a *lower* slot than the fan, so the fan read the already-step-lifted Y, putting Sonic inside the fan's vertical trigger range (`dy = playerY + $60 - fanY`, in-range `0 <= dy < $70`) one frame early and applying the +2px wind push a frame before ROM. - **S1 leftward horizontal camera scroll is uncapped (SYZ/all S1 zones):** the camera's per-frame horizontal scroll cap now applies only to *rightward* movement in Sonic 1, matching the shipped ROM. S1's `ScrollHoriz` caps the rightward move at 16px (`SH_MoveCameraRight`, unconditional) but the *leftward* cap (`SH_MoveCameraLeft`) is gated behind `if FixBugs`, and the shipped ROM has `FixBugs = 0` (`docs/s1disasm/sonic.asm:20`), so the left branch runs straight to `.moveLeft` and adds the full offset with no per-frame limit (`docs/s1disasm/_inc/ScrollHoriz & ScrollVertical.asm:59-99`). S2 (`s2.asm:18102-18105`) and S3K (`sonic3k.asm:38403-38406`) cap *both* directions, so this is an S1-only divergence. The engine's shared `Camera.computeNextHorizontalCameraX` capped both directions, so whenever Sonic moved left faster than 16px/frame the camera lagged ROM. At S1 SYZ1 trace f816 Sonic rides a leftward-moving FloatingBlock then springs back; the camera needed to move -17px left in one frame but the engine capped it at -16, leaving `camera_x` 1px right of ROM (0x0194 vs 0x0193) and cascading every subsequent camera_x frame. Fix: a `PhysicsFeatureSet.uncappedLeftwardHorizontalScroll` flag (true for `SONIC_1`, false for `SONIC_2`/`SONIC_3K`), plumbed to `Camera.setUncappedLeftwardScroll` from `LevelManager` alongside the existing `fastScrollCap` wiring, gating only the leftward branch. (The earlier "FloatingBlock riding miss" hypothesis was wrong — Sonic's kinematics matched ROM every frame; the 1px camera_x was a pure horizontal-scroll-cap symptom.) Advances the S1 SYZ1 complete-run frontier **f816 -> f2338** (360 -> 359 errors; the new f2338 root is an unrelated `x_speed` physics divergence) and additionally reduces the S1 MZ1 cascade (f2101 frontier, 204 -> 169 errors, same first-error frame) since MZ1 also has fast-leftward camera moments. Shared `Camera`/`PhysicsFeatureSet` change but regression-free: GHZ1/GHZ2 stay GREEN, every other S1 complete-run frontier frame+count byte-identical (LZ1 f5745/662, GHZ3 f6464/271, SLZ2 f2552/137, SBZ1 f3971/560, SYZ3 f6065/483), S2 EHZ1 PASS, S3K AIZ f1095/4309 unchanged, and `TestPhysicsProfile`/`TestPhysicsProfileRegression`/`TestCamera`/`TestCameraRewindSnapshot`/`TestLookScrollDelay`/`TestCollisionModel` (97 tests) all pass.

The base `out_of_range` macro deletes when the chunk-aligned reference X is more than 640 px right of the window's left edge (`cmpi.w #128+320+192,d0 / bhi exit`). In **act 3 only**, both conveyors' out-of-range tail does NOT immediately delete on that `bhi`: `LabyrinthConvey`/`SpinConvey` first run `cmpi.b #act3,(v_act).w` and, when in act 3, `cmpi.w #-$80,d0 / bhs.s LCon_Display` (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/63 LZ Conveyor.asm:16-20`; `docs/s1disasm/_incObj/6F SBZ Spin Platform Conveyor.asm:17-21`), so a platform whose aligned baseX (`objoff_30`) is up to one chunk (0x80) to the LEFT of the window (`d0 in [0xFF80,0xFFFF]`) is kept alive and displayed instead of deleted. Modelled on the ROM act value (a `cmpi.b #act3` ROM-state branch, the same object using the standard window in acts 1/2), via a new shared `AbstractObjectInstance.isInRangeAtWithLeftExtension(referenceX, leftChunks)` that mirrors the `bhs #-(leftChunks*$80)` keep. ROM `Saw_Action` ends with `out_of_range.s .delete, saw_origX(a0)` (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/6A SBZ Saws and Pizza Cutters.asm:39`), deleting the saw when its ORIGIN anchor (`saw_origX`, objoff_3A) leaves the camera window — checked AFTER the type subroutine runs (and, for ground saws, updates `saw_origX` to the moved `obX`, lines 338/400 = ROM `move.w obX(a0),saw_origX(a0)`). - **S1 badnik out_of_range unload runs AFTER the routine (post-move), via `checksOutOfRangeAfterRoutine()` (LZ + all S1 zones):** the S1 counter-based exec loop (`ObjectManager.updateCounterBasedExecThenLoad`) now defers the `out_of_range` unload check to *after* `executeObjectWithSolidContext` for objects whose ROM routine checks out_of_range at the END (post-move). A new `ObjectInstance.checksOutOfRangeAfterRoutine()` predicate (default `false`) is overridden to `true` on `AbstractBadnikInstance`: S1 badniks run `SpeedToPos` then `bra.w RememberState`, and `RememberState` tests the object's CURRENT post-move `x_pos` (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/sub RememberState.asm:9`; tails for Jaws `2C:58-59`, Crabmeat `1F:116,53`, Chopper `2B:35,11`, Burrobot `2D:70,42`, Moto Bug `40:89,67`, Newtron `42:129,38`, Roller `43:124,51`, Yadrin `50:110,88`, Ball Hog `1E,20:55`, Basaran `55:130`, Walking Bomb `5F:167,158`, Orbinaut `60:196,122`). When the predicate is true the loop SKIPS the pre-execute check and re-checks out_of_range post-execute, on the moved position; otherwise (static scenery / fixed-anchor objects whose ROM out_of_range is at routine START) the pre-execute check is kept unchanged. Previously the pre-execute check tested the PREVIOUS frame's position, so a moving badnik that left the camera window unloaded one frame late: at LZ2 the slot-37 Jaws (`@012F,0430`, `x_vel=-0x40`) is `object_removed` by ROM at f196 (aux) but the engine kept it until f197, holding a slot ROM had freed and drifting later `FindFreeObj` allocations. - **S1 conveyor platform survives its spawn frame before lazy baseX init (LZ/SBZ):** the LZ Conveyor (Obj 63, `Sonic1LZConveyorObjectInstance`) and SBZ Spin Conveyor (Obj 6F, `Sonic1SpinConveyorObjectInstance`) platforms no longer self-cull on the frame their spawner creates them. ROM `LabyrinthConvey` runs the routine dispatch (`LCon_Main`, which reads the path table and writes `objoff_30`=baseX) **before** the trailing `out_of_range.s loc_1236A,objoff_30(a0)` macro (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/63 LZ Conveyor.asm:5-13,53-63`; SBZ `SpinC_Main` is identical, `docs/s1disasm/_incObj/6F SBZ Spin Platform Conveyor.asm:5-13,37-54`), so a freshly spawned platform always has a valid `objoff_30` when its first `out_of_range` check runs. The engine loads `baseX` lazily in `ensureInitialized()` on the first `update()`; until then `baseX` is the sentinel `0`, and the object's `isPersistent()` (which mirrors ROM `out_of_range` via `isInRangeAt(baseX)`) returned false for any uninitialized platform whose spawn cluster the exec loop's out-of-range pre-pass reached before the platform's own first routine ran. Returning `true` from `isPersistent()` while `!initialized` (the platform initializes on its update this frame; the next frame's check uses the real baseX) keeps the ROM "routine sets objoff_30 before out_of_range" invariant. Advances the S1 LZ1 complete-run frontier from a `camera_y` symptom at f5745 to a 1px `y` landing residual at the same frame (**2214 -> 662 errors**; the residual is a sub-pixel corner-rounding phase on one of the three left-side ascending platforms — two of the three match ROM byte-for-byte, the lead one is 1px/1frame ahead). Regression-free: every other S1 complete-run frontier byte-identical (LZ2 f1068, LZ3 f7952, SBZ1 f3971, MZ2 f2819, MZ3 f2079, SBZ2 f1000, SLZ1 f164, SLZ2 f137, SLZ3 f1024, SYZ1 f360, SYZ3 f483, GHZ3 f6464, MZ1 f2089), GHZ1/GHZ2/SYZ2 stay GREEN, and `CollisionSystemTest`, `TestSolidRoutineProfiles`, `TestSonic1PlatformObjectInstanceRespawn`, `TestRewindCoverageGuard`, S3K `TestS3kAiz1SkipHeadless`/`TestSonic3kLevelLoading` all pass.
- **Camera bottom-boundary airborne acceleration reaches the camera one frame later (all games, MZ):** the camera's bottom-boundary easing (`Camera.updateBoundaryEasing` / `updatePosition`) now defers the airborne +8px boundary acceleration to the camera clamp by one frame, matching ROM ordering. ROM `DeformLayers` runs `ScrollVertical` (camera move + clamp to the current `v_limitbtm2`) **before** `DynamicLevelEvents` (`docs/s1disasm/_inc/DeformLayers (REV01).asm:16-18`), and `.move_boundary_down` accelerates the bottom boundary from +2px to +8px/frame once Sonic is airborne and the camera is within 8px of it (`docs/s1disasm/_inc/DynamicLevelEvents.asm:35-49`). Because the boundary update runs *after* the camera move, that +8 rate change is not visible to the camera until the next frame's `ScrollVertical`. The engine eases boundaries *before* moving the camera (`updateBoundaryEasing()` then `updatePosition()`), which is harmless while the boundary descends at a constant rate but applied the freshly-accelerated boundary to the same frame's camera clamp — running the +8 one frame early at the ground→air transition. At S1 MZ1 trace f2089 (Sonic going airborne, camera pinned to the descending bottom boundary), the engine jumped the camera to `0x02C4` while ROM was still at `0x02BE` (+6px early). Fix: a derived `cameraClampMaxY` that the camera clamp consumes, advancing in the boundary-descending direction by the step `maxY` took on the *previous* frame — so a constant +2 keeps perfect pace, but the +8 jump reaches the camera one frame late exactly like ROM. The ascending/snap path (ROM `SV_BottomBoundaryMoving`, GHZ2's rising boundary under a roll) still follows `maxY` same-frame, so GHZ2 stays green. `cameraClampMaxY` is derived (re-synced on `setMaxY` and reset to the converged value on rewind restore), so it needs no `CameraSnapshot` field. Advances the S1 MZ1 complete-run frontier **f2089 -> f2101** (205 -> 204 errors; the new f2101 root is a deeper boundary-easing-convergence divergence — the engine's `maxY` itself diverges from ROM `v_limitbtm2`, which needs the recorder to capture `v_limitbtm2` to resolve). Shared `Camera` change but regression-free: GHZ1/GHZ2 stay GREEN, every other S1 complete-run frontier byte-identical (LZ1 f5745, GHZ3 f6464, SLZ1 f2872, SYZ1 f816), S2 EHZ1 + S3K AIZ (f1095) unchanged, and `TestCamera`/`TestCameraRewindSnapshot`/`TestLookScrollDelay` pass.
- **S1 Seesaw tilt target computed post-player, atomic with the frame advance (SLZ):** the SLZ Seesaw (Obj 5E, `Sonic1SeesawObjectInstance`) now computes its tilt target (`See_ChkSide`) inside `update()` immediately before the `See_ChgFrame` mapping-frame advance, instead of latching it in `onSolidContact`. ROM `See_Slope2` (routine 4, `docs/s1disasm/_incObj/5E SLZ Seesaw.asm:71-118`) runs `See_ChkSide` (sets `see_frame` from the player's current x, then falls into `See_ChgFrame`) entirely inside `ExecuteObjects`, AFTER the player slot has moved. The engine runs S1 objects after player physics (`objectsExecuteAfterPlayerPhysics=true`), so `update()` already observes Sonic's post-move x — but the target was being latched in `onSolidContact`, which fires during the player's solid pass (BEFORE the post-physics object update), so `See_ChgFrame` advanced `obFrame` using the PREVIOUS frame's target. As the player rocked across the seesaw, the engine's tilt flip (`obFrame` 0x02→0x01 when the rocking player crossed within 8px of centre) lagged ROM by a frame, re-seating the rider on the stale (tilted) slope: at SLZ3 trace f745 ROM's seesaw is flat (`obj_frame=0x01`, confirmed by the v3.5 recorder `object_near` aux) and seats Sonic at y=0x02D8, while the engine still had it tilted (`0x02`) and seated him 3px low at 0x02DB; the lag also shifted the spikeball launch (f786). Moving `See_ChkSide` into `update()` (gated on the standing bit, which `onSolidContact` still maintains) keeps the ROM `ChkSide→ChgFrame` order atomic and post-move. Advances the S1 SLZ3 complete-run frontier **f745 -> f814** (resolving the f745/f756 tilt re-seat blips AND the f786 spikeball-launch cascade; the new f814 root is a deeper spikeball launch `y_speed` divergence). Regression-free: SLZ1 (f2872) and SLZ2 (f1714) byte-identical, MZ3 (f2079) unchanged, GHZ1/GHZ2/SYZ2/SBZ3 stay GREEN, and `TestSeesawBallGraphRewind`, `TestS1SlzBossSpikeballGraphRewind`, `TestSonic1LargeGrassyPlatformObjectInstance`, `TestCollisionLogic` all pass.

This keeps high-DPI/full-scaled windows from rendering the new mode into a small corner with the rest of the framebuffer black.

The engine still updates the logical render/projection width for widescreen profiles, but reshapes against the existing framebuffer so the OS window does not resize or jump position during title/game transitions.
